```
url: "https://github.com/gajtguy/splitflap-os"
finalUrl: "https://github.com/gajtguy/splitflap-os"
status: 200
contentType: text/html; charset=utf-8
title: "GitHub - gajtguy/splitflap-os: Reworked UI for Adam G's SplitFlap build · GitHub"
description: Reworked UI for Adam G's SplitFlap build. Contribute to gajtguy/splitflap-os development by creating an account on GitHub.
text: |
    SplitFlap OS
    A web-based control interface for modular split-flap displays. Manage apps, compose messages, and calibrate hardware from any device.
    Built on Adam G Makes' Split-Flap Display hardware platform.
    Features
    40+ apps — weather, stocks, sports scores, crypto, word clock, trivia, news headlines, quotes, and more
    App Library — browse and install apps by category (time, entertainment, news, lifestyle, education, finance, sports)
    Compose — click-to-type grid editor with color tile support
    Playlists — sequence apps and composed messages with per-entry timing and transitions
    Live preview — animated flap simulation in the browser
    Calibration tools — hardware inspector, auto fine-tune, teach mode
    MQTT — Home Assistant integration with auto-discovery
    WiFi hotspot fallback — Pi creates its own network when no WiFi is found, so you can always access the UI
    Offline resilience — internet-dependent apps degrade gracefully, offline apps keep running
    Plugin architecture — community apps via manifest + fetch pattern
    Mobile-friendly — hamburger menu, sticky bottom tabs, responsive layout
    Quick Start
    On your Split-Flap Display's Raspberry Pi:
    Raspberry Pi OS Lite users: git may not be pre-installed. Run this first:
    sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y git
    git clone https://github.com/csader/splitflap-os.git
    cd splitflap-os
    sudo bash setup/install.sh
    The installer sets up auto-start, WiFi hotspot fallback, and all dependencies. Access the UI at http://<your-pi-ip>.
    If no WiFi is available, the Pi creates a hotspot:
    SSID: SplitflapOS
    Password: splitflap
    UI: http://192.168.4.1
    Configure WiFi from Settings > WiFi / Network in the UI.
    Updating
    cd ~/splitflap-os
    git pull origin main
    sudo bash setup/install.sh
    Hardware
    This project is the web UI only. For the firmware and physical display hardware (3D printed parts, PCBs, BOM), see the original project by Adam G Makes:
    https://github.com/adamgmakes/SplitFlapDisplay
    Repo Structure
    server/ — Flask web app (backend + frontend)
    apps/ — Plugin library (all installable apps)
    setup/ — Raspberry Pi setup scripts and systemd services
    Creating an App
    Each app is a directory in apps/ with:
    manifest.json for metadata and settings schema
    app.py with a fetch(settings, format_lines, get_rows, get_cols) function
    fetch() returns a list of page strings. Each page shows for loop_delay seconds, and results are cached by refresh_interval.
    For full app-development documentation, settings schema, and examples, see APPS_README.md.
    Attribution
    Based on the Split-Flap Display by Adam G Makes, licensed under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
    License
    Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
    You are free to share and adapt this project for non-commercial purposes, as long as you give appropriate credit and distribute derivatives under the same license.
```

````

- path: README.md
  content: |
      # Split-Flap OS
      
      A Home Assistant custom integration for a split-flap display driven by the
      ESP32-C3 RS485 **SplitFlap Master** firmware. It replaces the older `splitflap`
      integration with a Home Assistant native app engine, a sidebar panel, and a
      tuning/calibration workbench.
      
      > 🇨🇿 Český návod pro začátečníky: [README.cs.md](README.cs.md).
      
      The integration talks to the master over MQTT. The master keeps ownership of the
      RS485 bus and the slave modules; Home Assistant owns text layout, apps, playlists,
      auto-detected board geometry, tuning state, and persistence.
      
      ```
      Home Assistant                         ESP32 master                 Slaves
      ┌───────────────────────────┐  MQTT    ┌──────────────┐   RS485     ┌────────┐
      │ Split-Flap OS integration │ ───────> │ command/*    │ ──────────> │ module │
      │ engine + apps + panel     │ <─────── │ status       │ <────────── │ module │
      └───────────────────────────┘          └──────────────┘             └────────┘
      ```
      
      ## Features
      
      - **Sidebar panel** (`Split-Flap OS`) with Control, Apps, Tuning, and Settings
        tabs, plus a live flap preview.
      - **Board auto-detection**: module count comes from the master status payload.
        45 modules become 3×15 and 64 become 4×16. Small displays use a single row.
        The physical frame can be overridden with rows/columns and a per-row module
        layout such as `3,3,1`.
      - **Physical layouts and app availability**: short rows are centred, module IDs
        are assigned in reading order, and data apps are disabled with a reason when
        every row is not wide enough.
      - **Apps** rendered from Home Assistant data where possible:
        clock, date, dashboard, weather, stocks, crypto, NHL scores, MBTA transit,
        countdown, world clock, ISS position, and colour animations.
      - **Playlists** with per-page text, loop control, and saved named playlists.
      - **Animation send orders**: left-to-right, right-to-left, columns, centre-out,
        outside-in, diagonal, random, rain, and spiral.
      - **Tuning UI** for module inspection, home, goto, relative steps, home offsets,
        EEPROM position maps, recording drum indexes, bus scan, sync, and refresh.
      - **Entities and services** so automations can send text, launch apps, and run
        hardware actions without the panel.
      - **Character validation**: text and playlists are checked against each
        module's reported `flap_list` before anything is sent; a missing flap raises
        an error naming the module and character.
      - **Czech localization** of the setup/options flow and service names; the panel
        and entity names remain English.
      - **Backup/restore** of settings, playlists, and the last module snapshot.
      - Only one config entry is allowed, matching the single-master firmware.
      
      ## Requirements
      
      - Home Assistant 2024.11 or newer.
      - The MQTT integration configured and connected to the broker used by the master.
      - SplitFlap Master firmware with these topics:
        - status: `<prefix>/status` (retained, JSON)
        - commands: `<prefix>/command/display`, `sync`, `scan`, `update`, `calibrate`
      - The default prefix is `splitflap`. It is configurable during setup.
      
      ## Installation
      
      ### HACS (custom repository)
      
      1. Add this repository as a HACS **Integration** custom repository.
      2. Install **Split-Flap OS**.
      3. Restart Home Assistant.
      4. Go to **Settings → Devices & services → Add integration → Split-Flap OS**.
      5. Enter the MQTT topic prefix (`splitflap` by default) and a display name.
      
      ### Manual
      
      Copy `custom_components/splitflap_os` into your Home Assistant
      `config/custom_components/` directory and restart. Then add the integration from
      the UI.
      
      The sidebar panel is registered automatically; no Lovelace resource entry is
      needed.
      
      ## Panel
      
      - **Control** — live display, multi-line compose box, colour insert buttons,
        start column, send order, speed, playlist builder, and saved playlists.
      - **Apps** — tap an app to start it; the gear opens the settings that app reads.
      - **Tuning** — module matrix, per-module diagnostics, motor home/goto/step,
        record and position-map controls, and a clickable character map.
      - **Settings** — grouped settings (display, weather, markets, sports, transit,
        time, animations), hardware actions, backup/restore, and connection details.
      
      The panel uses Home Assistant WebSocket commands and does not require a build
      step. It is loaded from `frontend/splitflap-os-panel.js` through `panel_custom`.
      
      ## Entities
      
      | Platform | Entity | Purpose |
      | --- | --- | --- |
      | sensor | Status | Master online/offline plus MQTT metadata |
      | sensor | Module count | Number of detected modules |
      | sensor | Display text | Last non-raw text shown |
      | sensor | Active app | Active app, playlist, or idle |
      | button | Home all | Home every module |
      | button | Scan bus | Full RS485 discovery |
      | button | Sync state | Republish master state / EEPROM sync |
      | button | Refresh modules | Update known modules without a scan |
      | button | Stop display | Stop the app or playlist |
      | text | Set display text | Write text directly from automations |
      | select | App | Start an app or choose Off |
      
      ## Services
      
      All services live under `splitflap_os.*`.
      
      | Service | Description |
      | --- | --- |
      | `send_text` | Send wrapped text with `start`, `style`, `speed`, `stop`, `raw` |
      | `play_playlist` | Play pages with `delay` and `loop` |
      | `start_app` / `stop_app` | Control the app engine |
      | `sync` / `scan` / `update` | Hardware state actions |
      | `calibrate` | Per-module goto/home/step/record/apply/clear_map/get_pos |
      | `home_all` / `record_all` | Bulk calibration helpers |
      | `save_playlist` / `delete_playlist` / `run_saved_playlist` | Playlist management |
      | `set_settings` | Merge and persist settings |
      
      Service `pages` fields accept a real YAML list when called from scripts, or a
      JSON array string when using the UI. `send_text` treats `start` as a 1-based
      column offset. `speed` is forwarded with the display command; the current master
      firmware ignores it and uses its own fixed bus timing.
      
      Before text is published, every module that reports a `flap_list` is checked
      for the characters it will receive. If a flap is missing, the service raises an
      error naming the module and character, and nothing is sent. `play_playlist`
      validates all pages before it starts. Padding spaces are ignored, and modules
      without a reported flap list are skipped because there is no drum to compare
      against.
      
      ## Settings
      
      Settings are stored with Home Assistant's `Store` under the config entry and are
      available from the panel. Important keys include:
      
      - `row_counts`, `rows`, `cols` — the physical display layout. `row_counts` is
        one comma-separated module count per row, for example `3,3,1`. Blank means
        automatic layout. `rows` and `cols` are the frame dimensions; `0` means
        derive them from the detected module count.
      - `ui_scale` — panel preview scale in percent (`50`–`200`, default `100`).
        Increase it to make a small physical display easier to see in the panel.
      - `timezone`, `units`, `page_delay`.
      - `weather_entity` (preferred), `zip_code` + `weather_api_key` (OpenWeather
        fallback).
      - `stocks_list`, `crypto_list`, `sports_teams`.
      - `metro_stop`, `metro_route`, `mbta_api_key`.
      - `countdown_event`, `countdown_target`, `clock_format`, `world_clock_zones`.
      - `anim_effect`, `anim_style`, `anim_speed`.
      
      Weather uses the Home Assistant `weather.get_forecasts` service when an entity is
      selected, so no external API key is required for the normal path. Stocks and
      crypto use Yahoo Finance and CoinGecko respectively. MBTA works without a key at
      low volume; an API key is optional.
      
      ## Physical layout and app availability
      
      The layout describes the real display, not just the number of modules.
      
      ```text
      row_counts = 3,3,1     frame = 3 rows × 3 columns
      
      row 1: module 1  module 2  module 3
      row 2: module 4  module 5  module 6
      row 3:          module 7
      ```
      
      Rules:
      
      - Module IDs are assigned left to right, then top to bottom.
      - A row with fewer modules is centred inside the frame.
      - A layout may leave blank frame cells, up to one row's worth. For example,
        7 modules in a 3×3 frame is valid; 7 modules in a 3×15 frame is rejected.
      - The integration rejects a saved layout that does not match the detected
        module count or leaves too much blank space. If the detected count changes
        later, the panel shows a layout error instead of silently using the wrong
        modules.
      - Text pages and colour animations work on any valid layout, including one
        module. Data apps require every row to be wide enough for their content.
      
      App minimums are declared in `apps/__init__.py`:
      
      | App | Minimum frame |
      | --- | --- |
      | Animations | any size |
      | Clock | 3 × 9 |
      | Date | 3 × 11 |
      | Dashboard | 3 × 11 |
      | Weather | 3 × 10 |
      | Stocks | 3 × 7 |
      | Crypto | 3 × 8 |
      | Sports | 3 × 8 |
      | Metro | 3 × 10 |
      | Countdown | 3 × 12 |
      | World Clock | 1 × 10 |
      | ISS | 3 × 10 |
      
      Unsupported app cards are disabled and show the requirement. Starting one from
      the panel or a service returns an error. If a running app becomes unsupported
      because the layout changed, the engine stops it.
      
      ## MQTT contract
      
      The integration expects the master's retained status payload to look like this
      (abridged):
      
      ```json
      {
        "state": "online",
        "text": "HELLO",
        "version": "1.1.0.0",
        "bus_compat": 1,
        "mqtt_compat": 1,
        "compat": 1,
        "modules_count": 45,
        "modules": [
          {
            "id": 1,
            "state": "online",
            "online": true,
            "flap": "H",
            "total_steps": 4096,
            "home_offset": 2832,
            "current_step": 3616,
            "flap_list": " ABC...",
            "map_of_positions": {"0": 2832, "1": 2896},
            "fw_version": "1.0.1",
            "fw_bus_compat": 1,
            "fw_bus_compatible": true,
            "fw_compat": 1,
            "fw_compatible": true
          }
        ]
      }
      ```
      
      `version`/`bus_compat`/`mqtt_compat` are the master's own version contract;
      `compat` remains an alias for `mqtt_compat` for older integration builds. The
      per-module `fw_version`/`fw_bus_compat` come from the slave's `m<id>s` reply;
      `fw_bus_compatible` is omitted when the module does not report a version, and
      `fw_compat`/`fw_compatible` remain aliases for the bus values.
      
      Display commands are sent as an ordered array so the array order doubles as the
      animation order:
      
      ```json
      {"modules": [{"id": 1, "char": "H"}, {"id": 2, "char": "I"}]}
      ```
      
      Calibration commands use `{"module": 1, "action": "goto", "index": 5}` and the
      master translates them to the slave protocol.
      
      Position-map entries with the slave's `0xFFFF` sentinel are treated as unset:
      they are omitted from snapshots, never shown as tuned in the character map,
      and the integration falls back to the estimated flap position. Negative and
      out-of-range entries are ignored in the same way. An explicit `positions`
      object sent to the `calibrate` service may still contain `65535` to clear a
      single entry on the slave.
      
      ## Versions and module firmware
      
      All three parts of the system (slave firmware, ESP32 master, this integration)
      use two independent **compatibility axes** because two different peers talk to
      each other:
      
      | Axis | Peer contract | Carried by |
      | --- | --- | --- |
      | **BUS_COMPAT** | RS485 application protocol and the OTA/bootloader entry contract | slave + master |
      | **MQTT_COMPAT** | MQTT status/command JSON schema | master + Home Assistant |
      
      The master bridges the two, so it carries both numbers. Each repository also
      has its own release inside those generations, and the published version is
      composed from the numbers that apply to it:
      
      ```
      slave    <bus>.<release>              1.0.1      bus 1, release 0.1
      master   <bus>.<mqtt>.<release>       1.1.0.0    bus 1, mqtt 1, release 0.0
      HA       <mqtt>.<release>             1.0.8      mqtt 1, release 0.8
      ```
      
      | Where | Version | Compatibility | Read from |
      | --- | --- | --- | --- |
      | Home Assistant integration | `1.0.8` | MQTT `1` | panel header, connection info, WebSocket `version`/`mqtt_compat` |
      | ESP32 master | `1.1.0.0` | bus `1`, MQTT `1` | status `version`/`bus_compat`/`mqtt_compat`, connection info |
      | Slave application | `1.0.1` | bus `1` | panel module inspector, firmware card, `m<id>v`, UPDI dump |
      
      The integration compares the master's `mqtt_compat` with `MQTT_COMPAT` in
      `const.py`. A mismatch shows a warning banner, but it never blocks display
      traffic, OTA cancellation or a module reset. If the master predates the version
      protocol, the panel says the version is unknown rather than assuming it is
      compatible. The bus generation is shown for diagnostics; the slave <-> master
      side is not something Home Assistant speaks directly.
      
      The module firmware card shows the application version and bus generation each
      slave reports. Use it to prove an OTA actually took: bump the slave's
      `FW_RELEASE`, upload the new `.hex`, and the card should show the new version
      after the module reboots and re-homes. OTA itself refuses an unknown bootloader
      protocol before writing any page.
      
      When changing the frontend, bump `VERSION` in `const.py`, `manifest.json` and
      `frontend/constants.js`, and every `?v=` import parameter, together.
      `tests/test_versions.py` enforces that lockstep and the major/MQTT_COMPAT
      relationship.
      
      ## Coordinate system and recording index 0
      
      The slave counts `pos` from the hall entering edge. Flap 0 sits at `homeOffset`,
      and the fallback position for an unset map entry is
      `homeOffset + round(index * totalStepsPerRev / 64)`, modulo
      `totalStepsPerRev`. The integration mirrors this when it estimates a flap
      position, so `home_offset` and `total_steps` in the status payload are enough to
      locate any flap.
      
      Recording index 0 is supported: `m<id>r0` stores the current position as
      `map[0]` and redefines `homeOffset`. That is the intended way to re-centre flap
      0, not a destructive compatibility write. Older master firmware also sent a
      second `m<id>w0:0`; current firmware does not.
      
      ## Adding an app
      
      1. Add an async provider in `custom_components/splitflap_os/apps/`:
      
         ```python
         async def my_app(engine, now) -> list[Page]:
             return [Page(engine.lines("HELLO", "WORLD", ""), delay=5)]
         ```
      
      2. Describe it with `AppDef` and register it in
         `custom_components/splitflap_os/apps/__init__.py`.
      3. If it has settings, add `SettingField`s and optionally add them to a group in
         `settings.py`.
      
      Providers are called once per display cycle. Slow network calls should use
      `await engine.async_cached(key, ttl, factory)`.
      
      ## Project layout
      
      ```
      custom_components/splitflap_os/
      ├── __init__.py          setup, unload, cleanup
      ├── apps/                app providers and registry
      ├── config_flow.py       single-instance setup and options
      ├── const.py             domain constants
      ├── coordinator.py       MQTT state, normalization, publishing
      ├── engine.py            display loop, playlists, settings, backup
      ├── entity.py            shared entity base
      ├── frontend/            sidebar panel JavaScript
      ├── layout.py            pure text/layout/order/rotation helpers
      ├── manifest.json
      ├── models.py            Page object
      ├── panel.py             static path + panel registration
      ├── runtime.py           runtime lookup helper
      ├── sensor.py / button.py / text.py / select.py
      ├── services.py / services.yaml
      ├── settings.py          grouped settings metadata
      ├── strings.json / translations/en.json
      └── websocket_api.py     panel commands
      ```
      
      `app.py` and `index.html` in the repository root are AdamGMakes' original
      reference implementation. They are not loaded by Home Assistant.
      
      ## Development checks
      
      Home Assistant is not vendored in this repository. Run the checks that do not
      need a full Home Assistant install:
      
      ```bash
      python3 -m py_compile custom_components/splitflap_os/*.py \
        custom_components/splitflap_os/apps/*.py
      for f in $(find custom_components/splitflap_os/frontend -name '*.js'); do node --check "$f"; done
      python3 -m json.tool custom_components/splitflap_os/manifest.json >/dev/null
      python3 -m json.tool custom_components/splitflap_os/strings.json >/dev/null
      python3 tests/test_layout.py
      python3 tests/test_positions.py
      python3 tests/test_translations.py
      python3 tests/test_ota.py
      python3 tests/test_versions.py
      ```
      
      ## Credits
      
      This project builds on the original **Split-Flap Display** design by
      **Adam G Makes** ([@adamgmakes](https://github.com/adamgmakes)):
      
      - Repository: https://github.com/adamgmakes/SplitFlapDisplay
      - The 3D-printed module hardware, drum/character set, RS485 bus protocol,
        and the reference Python frontend in this repository's root (`app.py`,
        `index.html`) are derived from that work.
      
      The original project is licensed under
      [Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International
      (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/).
      This derivative is shared on the same terms: non-commercial use, attribution to
      Adam G Makes, and any further derivatives distributed under the same license.
      Commercial use requires permission from the original author.
      
      ## Troubleshooting
      
      - **Panel says OFFLINE** — check the MQTT integration, the topic prefix, and the
        retained `<prefix>/status` payload. The master sends a heartbeat every 30
        seconds; the integration marks it offline after 90 seconds.
      - **No modules** — press **Scan bus** in Tuning. The status payload's
        `modules_count` drives the board size.
      - **Layout error or disabled apps** — open Settings and adjust the frame or
        row layout. A row layout such as `3,3,1` must describe every detected module
        and may leave at most one row of blank frame cells. Data apps stay disabled
        until every row is wide enough.
      - **Display shows old text after a restart** — the integration restores the last
        known module snapshot and desired characters; press **Sync** to refresh from
        the master.
      - **Service fails with "Cannot display: module ... lacks ..."** — a module's
        reported drum lacks one of the requested characters. Check the module in
        Tuning, use a character from its flap list, or remove it. Nothing was sent to
        the display.
      - **Panel missing after install** — reload the integration once, then hard-refresh
        the browser. Check Home Assistant logs for `panel` or static-path errors.
````

```
    # ============================================================

    def send_raw(cmd):
    if not cmd.endswith('\n'):
    cmd += '\n'
    with serial_lock:
    if ser and not sim_mode:
    ser.write(cmd.encode())
    ser.flush()
    time.sleep(0.02)
    def sync_hardware_data(mod_id):
    if not ser:
    return False
    with serial_lock:
    ser.reset_input_buffer()
    ser.write(f"m{mod_id:02d}d\n".encode())
    ser.flush()
    start = time.time()
    buffer = ""
    target = f"m{mod_id:02d}d:"
    while time.time() - start < 5.0:
    if ser.in_waiting > 0:
    try:
    chunk = ser.read(ser.in_waiting).decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    buffer += chunk
    if target in buffer and '\n' in buffer[buffer.find(target):]:
    valid_part = buffer[buffer.find(target):].split('\n')[0]
    data = valid_part.split('d:', 1)[1]
    parts = data.split(':')
    if len(parts) >= 2:
    settings['offsets'][str(mod_id)] = int(parts[0])
    settings['calibrations'][str(mod_id)] = int(parts[1])
    settings['tuned_chars'][str(mod_id)] = {}
    if len(parts) == 3 and parts[2]:
    for p in parts[2].split(','):
    if '=' in p:
    idx, val = p.split('=')
    settings['tuned_chars'][str(mod_id)][idx] = int(val)
    save_settings(settings)
    return True
    except Exception as e:
    logging.error(f"Parse error: {e}")
    time.sleep(0.05)
    return False
    # ============================================================
    # ANIMATION ORDER GENERATORS
    # ============================================================
    def get_animation_order(style='ltr', rows=None, cols=None):
    """Return a list of the module indices in the requested send order."""
    rows = rows or get_rows()
    cols = cols or get_cols()
    total = rows * cols
    def m(r, c): return r * cols + c
    if style == 'rtl':
    return list(range(total - 1, -1, -1))
    elif style == 'center_out':
    order, seen = [], set()
    center = cols // 2
    for d in range(center + 1):
    for r in range(rows):
    cs = [center] if d == 0 else [center - d, center + d]
    for c in cs:
    if 0 <= c < cols:
    idx = m(r, c)
    if idx not in seen:
    seen.add(idx); order.append(idx)
    return order
    elif style == 'outside_in':
    return list(reversed(get_animation_order('center_out', rows, cols)))
    elif style == 'spiral':
    vis = [[False] * cols for _ in range(rows)]
    order = []
    top, bottom, left, right = 0, rows - 1, 0, cols - 1
    while top <= bottom and left <= right:
    for c in range(left, right + 1):
    if not vis[top][c]:
    vis[top][c] = True; order.append(m(top, c))
    for r in range(top + 1, bottom + 1):
    if not vis[r][right]:
    vis[r][right] = True; order.append(m(r, right))
    if top < bottom:
    for c in range(right - 1, left - 1, -1):
    if not vis[bottom][c]:

    seen.add(idx); order.append(idx)
    return order

    return [m(r, c) for r in range(rows) for c in range(cols)]

    return [m(r, c) for r in range(rows - 1, -1, -1) for c in range(cols)]

    def send_to_display(text, order=None, raw=False, step_delay_ms=15):
    global current_indices, current_display_string, is_homed
    if not text:
    return 0
    # For normal text: uppercase first (emojis are unaffected by upper()),
    # then replace emojis with color codes. Animation pages pass raw=True to
    # skip uppercasing so their color codes (r o y g b p w) stay lowercase.
    if not raw:
    clean_text = text.upper()
    else:
    clean_text = text
    for emoji, char in COLOR_MAP.items():
    clean_text = clean_text.replace(emoji, char)
    # Apply currency symbol alias: user's currency char → $ (the physical flap position)
    currency = settings.get('currency_symbol', '$').strip()
    if currency and currency != '$':
    clean_text = clean_text.replace(currency.upper(), '$')
    # The physical " flap is addressed as 'q' in the firmware character map
    clean_text = clean_text.replace('"', 'q')
    n = get_module_count()
    clean_text = clean_text.ljust(n)[:n]
    logging.info(f"DISPLAY: {clean_text}")
    if order is None:
    order = list(range(n))
    max_dist = 0
    with serial_lock:
    for i in order:
    if i >= len(clean_text):
    continue
    char = clean_text[i]
    if ser and not sim_mode:
    ser.write(f"m{i:02d}-{char}\n".encode())
    ser.flush()
    time.sleep(step_delay_ms / 1000.0)
    target_idx = FLAP_CHARS.find(char)
    if target_idx == -1:
    target_idx = 0
    dist = 128 if current_indices[i] == -1 else (target_idx - current_indices[i]) % 64
    if dist > max_dist:
    max_dist = dist
    current_indices[i] = target_idx
```

> _Reasoning_
> Now I have a clear picture. Key differences:
> 
> gajtguy/splitflap-os:
> - A fork (9 commits behind? Actually fork updated May 30 2026, parent last pushed Oct 21 2026 — fork is stale ~5 months).
> - Flask web server on Raspberry Pi connected directly to display over USB serial (/dev/ttyUSB0, 9600 baud), i.e., uses Adam's original serial protocol with `mXX<char>` commands.
> - Single 84KB server/app.py monolith, no tests, no typing, no modular architecture.
> - 40+ apps as installable plugins (manifest.json + app.py fetch()) fetched from app library URL at runtime.
> - Home Assistant integration via MQTT discovery only (text, select app, select playlist, switch center, sensors), not a custom component. So it lives alongside HA, not inside it.
> - WiFi hotspot fallback, Pi setup scripts/systemd.
> - App library install/uninstall from remote GitHub, arbitrary Python execution (security note).
> - Fixed 45 modules in some places; grid based on sim_rows/sim_cols settings, no auto-detect or ragged row layout.
> - Version file single number, no compat axes.
> - No OTA, no slave firmware handling, no calibration position maps beyond offsets/calibrations/tuned_chars.
> - i18n English only.
> 
> Yours:
> - Native HA custom integration, one config entry, MQTT to ESP32 master (master owns RS485).
> - Coordinator/engine separation, websocket API, entities & services, panel via panel_custom, no build step, bilingual EN/CS.
> - Physical layout with ragged rows, per-row counts, app min rows/cols gating.
> - Firmware/OTA for slaves (base64 image chunks, bootloader protocol version).
> - Compat axes MQTT_COMPAT/BUS_COMPAT, tests enforcing versions, pure modules unit tested.
> - 10k lines code, tests.
> - Requires ESP32 master firmware; remote directly drives homemade serial bus via Pi UART.
> 
> Is it "better"? Answer: they're not substitutes. Depends on hardware. gajtguy better at: app breadth (40+ plugins, installable app library), standalone Pi deployment, WiFi hotspot fallback, plugin ecosystem with manifest-driven settings, more sports leagues, notification interrupts, teach mode/auto fine-tune, live preview animation. But its code quality/maintainability is much weaker: monolith, no tests, no type hints, hard-coded 45 defaults, security risk of executing arbitrary plugins, fork stale relative to upstream.
> 
> Let me verify some claims about their calibration/teach mode and preview quickly? README claims. Also the local repo may already have some of those. Let me check local apps registry to list apps, and whether local has notification, teach mode, etc. Quick grep.

I read the repo, its file tree, and its server code, and compared it to your integration. Short answer: **it isn't a newer or better version of your project — it's a different product for a different hardware topology.** It's also a stale fork of `csader/splitflap-os` (fork last pushed May 30, 2026; upstream Oct 21, 2026), so even as a "competitor" you should look at the parent repo, not this fork.

## What it actually is

`gajtguy/splitflap-os` is a **standalone Flask web UI that runs on a Raspberry Pi and drives the modules directly over USB serial** (`/dev/ttyUSB0`, 9600 baud, `m01-A` style commands, `send_raw()` in `server/app.py`). It is AdamGMakes' original control path with a much richer web front end. Home Assistant is an afterthought: it publishes MQTT discovery configs for a text entity, app/playlist selects, a center switch and some sensors.

Yours is the opposite split: **Home Assistant owns layout, apps, playlists, persistence and the UI; an ESP32 master owns the RS485 bus**; MQTT is the contract in between.

That means they aren't interchangeable. On your hardware (ESP32 master + RS485 slaves) the Flask app would bypass the master and need the Pi physically wired to the bus. The two are mutually exclusive owners of the same display.

## Where it is genuinely ahead of yours

1. **App ecosystem.** ~40 installable apps vs your 12. Each app is a directory with `manifest.json` + `app.py` exposing `fetch(settings, format_lines, get_rows, get_cols)`, and the UI can install them from a remote app library (`app_library_url`). It has content apps you don't: BirdNET, YouTube/livestream comments, moon phase, word clock, art clock, dad jokes, quotes, magic 8-ball, fortune cookie, etc., plus far more sports leagues (17 vs NHL-only).
2. **Plugin-shaped settings schema.** `manifest.json` declares fields, visibility, dependent fields (`visible_when`, `disabled_when`), computed values and inline toggles; the server builds the settings UI from that. Yours uses hand-written `SettingField`s and a settings registry.
3. **Notification interrupts.** A queue that overlays a message on top of whatever app is running, then resumes.
4. **Deployment ergonomics.** `setup/install.sh`, systemd services, and **WiFi hotspot fallback** (`SplitflapOS` / `http://192.168.4.1`) so the UI is always reachable. Yours depends on HA and the broker being up.
5. **Runs with no hardware.** It auto-enters simulation mode when the serial port is missing, with configurable `sim_rows`/`sim_cols` — handy for developing app content.
6. **Calibration UX.** Claims auto fine-tune and a "teach mode", plus tuned-character maps per module in the browser.

## Where yours is clearly better

1. **Code architecture.** Theirs is one 84 KB `server/app.py` with module-level globals, no typing, no separation of transport/state/UI, and threaded timing loops. Yours has coordinator/engine/apps/layout/positions/websocket boundaries, typed Python, and `snapshot()` as a state contract.
2. **Nothing is tested.** No `tests/` directory at all. Yours has layout/positions/translations/OTA/version tests, including the compat-axis enforcement.
3. **Physical layout correctness.** Theirs is a rigid `rows * cols` grid derived from `sim_rows`/`sim_cols`, with `45` hard-coded as the default module count and offsets/calibrations. Yours auto-detects module count, supports ragged rows (`3,3,1`), centres short rows, validates blank cells, and gates apps by `min_rows`/`min_cols` against the narrowest row.
4. **Firmware awareness.** Yours handles slave OTA (`ota.py`, `firmware.py`, base64 chunk publishing), bootloader protocol checking, per-module firmware reporting, and the master/slave version contract. Theirs has a single `VERSION` file and no concept of module firmware.
5. **HA-native surface.** Yours gives a config flow, one-entry enforcement, entities, services (`send_text`, `calibrate`, playlists, backup/restore), and a `panel_custom` sidebar panel. Theirs only gets MQTT-discovery entities and has no HA services.
6. **Security.** Their plugin loader `exec_module`s arbitrary Python downloaded from GitHub, and the code comments say so explicitly. Your app registry is static and reviewed.
7. **Bilingual UI.** EN + CS throughout; theirs is English-only.
8. **Cache/version discipline.** Your lockstep `VERSION` + `?v=` + `MQTT_COMPAT` rule is more robust than their single `VERSION` file and Flask static assets.

## Verdict

- **Do not switch.** For your stack (ESP32 master, RS485, HA-native), yours is the better-engineered system and is the only one that speaks your MQTT contract, layout rules, OTA path and compat axes. Their project would require a Pi on the bus and would throw away the master firmware design.
- **Do borrow selectively**, if any of it matters to you:
  - a manifest-driven app definition so a third-party app can be dropped in without editing `apps/__init__.py`;
  - a notification overlay queue (high value for HA automations — "someone's at the door" over a running clock);
  - a no-hardware simulation mode with a configurable grid;
  - teach mode / auto fine-tune for calibration.
- If you want to see the maintained version of that project, look at **`csader/splitflap-os`** (10 stars, 6 forks, 3 open issues) — the `gajtguy` copy is five months behind.

No files were changed; this was a read-only comparison of the remote repo against your `custom_components/splitflap_os`.

````
text: |
    # App Development Guide
    For high-level project setup, usage, and hardware notes, see [README.md](README.md).
    ## Build Your First App
    Each app lives under `apps/<app-id>/` and typically has two files.
    **manifest.json**
    ```json
    {
    "id": "my-app",
    "name": "My App",
    "icon": "🎯",
    "description": "What it does",
    "category": "entertainment",
    "type": "functional",
    "refresh_interval": 60,
    "loop_delay": 5,
    "settings": []
    }
    ```
    **app.py**
    ```python
    def fetch(settings, format_lines, get_rows, get_cols):
    return [format_lines("LINE 1", "LINE 2", "LINE 3")]
    ```
    How runtime behavior works:
    - `fetch()` returns a list of page strings.
    - Each page is shown for `loop_delay` seconds.
    - Fetch results are cached for `refresh_interval` seconds.
    ## Define Settings in manifest.json
    `manifest.json` `settings` supports these field `type` values:
    - `text`, `number`, `password`, `datetime-local`, `textarea`
    - `select` with `options`
    - `search_chips` with `searchUrl`, `resultKey`, and optional `maxItems`
    - `toggle` with `options` (segmented control)
    - `computed` with `compute` and `watches` (read-only derived info)
    Common optional keys:
    - `number`: `min`, `max`, `step`, optional `stepper: true`
    - `toggle`: optional `size` (`"sm"`, `"md"`, `"lg"`)
    - Any field: `visible_when` for conditional show/hide
    For `select` and `toggle`, options can be either:
    - string form: `"MI"`
    - object form: `{ "value": "mi", "label": "MI" }`
    ## Recommended Minimal Pattern
    Use this structure for most new apps:
    ```json
    {
    "settings": [
    {
    "key": "units",
    "label": "Units",
    "type": "toggle",
    "default": "imperial",
    "options": [
    { "value": "imperial", "label": "Imperial" },
    { "value": "metric", "label": "Metric" }
    ]
    },
    {
    "key": "refresh_minutes",
    "label": "Refresh Minutes",
    "type": "number",
    "default": 15,
    "min": 1,
    "max": 60
    }
    ]
    }
    ```
    Conventions:
    - Use stable lowercase keys with underscores (example: `refresh_minutes`).
    - Always define a `default`.
    - Prefer object options (`value` + `label`) for `select` and `toggle`.
    - Only add sync rules when dependent behavior is needed.
    ## Add Optional Setting Features
    ### Number Stepper Buttons
    Add explicit `- / +` controls to a `number` field:
    ```json
    {
    "key": "polling_rate",
    "label": "Polling Rate (seconds)",
    "type": "number",
    "stepper": true,
    "default": 60,
    "min": 15,
    "max": 3600,
    "step": 15
    }
    ```
    ### Conditional Visibility
    Show a field only when other setting values match.
    - format: `{ "other_key": "expected_value" }`
    - multiple keys are combined with AND logic
    ```json
    {
    "key": "flightaware_api_key",
    "label": "FlightAware API Key",
    "type": "password",
    "default": "",
    "visible_when": { "data_source": "flightaware" }
    }
    ```
    ### Computed Read-Only Fields
    Render live derived text in settings:
    - `compute`: compute function name in frontend registry
    - `watches`: keys that trigger recomputation
    ```json
    {
    "key": "_polling_stats",
    "label": "API Usage Estimate",
    "type": "computed",
    "compute": "polling_rate_stats",
    "watches": ["polling_rate", "data_source"]
    }
    ```
    ### Inline Toggle Next to Input
    Attach a segmented toggle to a text/number field via `inline_toggle`:
    ```json
    {
    "key": "search_radius",
    "label": "Search Radius",
    "type": "number",
    "default": 100,
    "inline_toggle": {
    "key": "search_radius_unit",
    "options": [
    { "value": "mi", "label": "MI" },
    { "value": "km", "label": "KM" }
    ],
    "default": "mi",
    "position": "after",
    "size": "md"
    }
    }
    ```
    `inline_toggle` keys:
    - `key` (required): setting key persisted alongside the main input
    - `options` (required): string/object option list
    - `default` (optional): default selected option
    - `position` (optional): `"before"` or `"after"` (default)
    - `size` (optional): `"sm"`, `"md"`, or `"lg"`
    ### Declarative Settings Sync
    Use these keys to synchronize related fields:
    - `sync_values` on source field: maps source value to updates for target fields
    - `sync_parent` on child field: parent key to set when child changes manually
    - `sync_parent_custom_value` on child field: parent value to set (default: `"custom"`)
    ```json
    {
    "key": "units_preset",
    "type": "toggle",
    "options": ["aviation", "metric", "imperial", "custom"],
    "sync_values": {
    "aviation": {"distance_unit": "nm", "altitude_unit": "fl", "speed_unit": "kt"},
    "metric": {"distance_unit": "km", "altitude_unit": "m", "speed_unit": "kmh"},
    "imperial": {"distance_unit": "mi", "altitude_unit": "ft", "speed_unit": "mph"}
    }
    }
    ```
    ```json
    {
    "key": "distance_unit",
    "type": "toggle",
    "sync_parent": "units_preset",
    "sync_parent_custom_value": "custom"
    }
    ```
    ## Final Checklist
    - Confirm your app directory contains `manifest.json` and `app.py`.
    - Ensure every setting has a stable `key` and sensible `default`.
    - Use `visible_when` and sync rules only when they improve UX.
    - Keep `fetch()` fast and resilient to network/API errors.
    ## Optional: Lucide Icon in Settings Modal
    The settings modal title uses the emoji from `manifest.json` by default. If you want a Lucide icon instead, add your app to the `LUCIDE_APP_ICONS` map in `server/static/app.js`:
    ```js
    const LUCIDE_APP_ICONS = {
    // ...existing entries...
    'my-app': 'plane', // any Lucide icon name
    };
    ```
    Browse available icons at [lucide.dev](https://lucide.dev). The emoji in `manifest.json` is still used as a fallback on app tiles and in the App Library.
````

```
  content: |
      """Metadata helpers for the app registry and settings UI."""
      
      from __future__ import annotations
      
      from dataclasses import dataclass
      from typing import Any
      
      
      @dataclass(frozen=True)
      class SettingField:
          """Description of one editable setting, rendered by the panel."""
      
          key: str
          label: str
          type: str = "text"
          options: tuple[str, ...] = ()
          placeholder: str = ""
          default: Any = ""
          minimum: float | None = None
          maximum: float | None = None
          step: float | None = None
          domain: str | None = None
          help: str = ""
      
          def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
              return {
                  "key": self.key,
                  "label": self.label,
                  "type": self.type,
                  "options": list(self.options),
                  "placeholder": self.placeholder,
                  "default": self.default,
                  "min": self.minimum,
                  "max": self.maximum,
                  "step": self.step,
                  "domain": self.domain,
                  "help": self.help,
              }
      
      
      @dataclass(frozen=True)
      class AppDef:
          """A runnable app shown on the Apps tab."""
      
          key: str
          name: str
          icon: str
          description: str
          fields: tuple[SettingField, ...] = ()
          default_delay: float = 5.0
          category: str = "data"
          min_rows: int = 1
          min_cols: int = 1
          modes: tuple[str, ...] = ()
      
          def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
              return {
                  "key": self.key,
                  "name": self.name,
                  "icon": self.icon,
                  "description": self.description,
                  "fields": [field.as_dict() for field in self.fields],
                  "default_delay": self.default_delay,
                  "category": self.category,
                  "min_rows": self.min_rows,
                  "min_cols": self.min_cols,
                  "modes": list(self.modes),
              }
      
      
      def split_csv(value: object) -> list[str]:
          """Split a comma-separated setting into clean values."""
      
          if value is None:
              return []
          return [part.strip() for part in str(value).split(",") if part.strip()]
      
      
      def as_float(value: object, default: float) -> float:
          try:
              return float(value)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
          except (TypeError, ValueError):
              return default
      
      
      def as_int(value: object, default: int = 0) -> int:
          try:
              return int(value)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
          except (TypeError, ValueError):
              return default
      
      
      def condition_label(condition: object) -> str:
          """Turn a Home Assistant weather condition into a short label."""
      
          key = str(condition or "").strip().lower()
          labels = {
              "clear": "CLEAR",
              "clear-night": "CLEAR",
              "cloudy": "CLOUDY",
              "exceptional": "ALERT",
              "fog": "FOG",
              "hail": "HAIL",
              "lightning": "STORMS",
              "lightning-rainy": "STORMS",
              "partlycloudy": "PARTLY CLOUDY",
              "pouring": "HEAVY RAIN",
              "rainy": "RAIN",
              "snowy": "SNOW",
              "snowy-rainy": "SLEET",
              "sunny": "SUNNY",
              "windy": "WINDY",
              "windy-variant": "WINDY",
          }
          return labels.get(key, key.upper() or "UNKNOWN")
      
      
      def compact_number(value: float, *, currency: str = "") -> str:
          """Format a price for a narrow split-flap row."""
      
          prefix = "$" if currency.upper() in {"USD", "US$", "$"} else ""
          absolute = abs(value)
          if absolute >= 10_000:
              return f"{prefix}{value:,.0f}"
          if absolute >= 1_000:
              return f"{prefix}{value:,.1f}"
          if absolute >= 1:
              return f"{prefix}{value:,.2f}"
          return f"{prefix}{value:.4f}"
      
      
      def signed_percent(value: float) -> str:
          return f"{value:+.2f}%"
      
- path: custom_components/splitflap_os/settings.py
  content: |
      """Settings metadata and defaults shared by the integration and the panel."""
      
      from __future__ import annotations
      
      from typing import Any
      
      from .apps import (
          ANIMATION_FIELDS,
          COUNTDOWN_FIELDS,
          CRYPTO_FIELDS,
          METRO_FIELDS,
          SPORTS_FIELDS,
          STOCK_FIELDS,
          WEATHER_FIELDS,
          WORLD_CLOCK_FIELDS,
      )
      from .apps.common import SettingField
      
      DISPLAY_FIELDS = (
          SettingField(
              key="row_counts",
              label="Physical row layout (blank = auto)",
              type="text",
              default="",
              placeholder="3,3,1",
              help=(
                  "One number per physical row, top to bottom. Module IDs are "
                  "assigned left to right, then top to bottom. Short rows are "
                  "centred. Blank lets the integration choose from the detected "
                  "module count."
              ),
          ),
          SettingField(
              key="rows",
              label="Frame rows (0 = auto)",
              type="number",
              default=0,
              minimum=0,
              maximum=100,
              step=1,
              help="Physical frame height. Leave 0 to derive it from the display.",
          ),
          SettingField(
              key="cols",
              label="Frame columns (0 = auto)",
              type="number",
              default=0,
              minimum=0,
              maximum=100,
              step=1,
              help="Physical frame width. Leave 0 to derive it from the display.",
          ),
          SettingField(
              key="ui_scale",
              label="Preview scale (%)",
              type="number",
              default=100,
              minimum=50,
              maximum=200,
              step=5,
              help=(
                  "Scales the flap and module previews in the panel. "
                  "100% is the default; use a larger value for small displays."
              ),
          ),
          SettingField(
              key="timezone",
              label="Timezone",
              type="timezone",
              placeholder="Home Assistant default",
              help="IANA name such as Europe/London. Empty uses Home Assistant's timezone.",
          ),
          SettingField(
              key="units",
              label="Units",
              type="select",
              options=("auto", "imperial", "metric"),
              default="auto",
          ),
          SettingField(
              key="page_delay",
              label="Default page delay (s)",
              type="number",
              default=5,
              minimum=0.1,
              maximum=120,
              step=0.5,
          ),
      )
      
      SETTINGS_GROUPS: list[dict[str, Any]] = [
          {
              "key": "display",
              "name": "Display",
              "icon": "🖥",
              # "category" routes the group to the panel's Display or Apps
              # settings sub-tab.
              "category": "display",
              "fields": [field.as_dict() for field in DISPLAY_FIELDS],
          },
          {
              "key": "weather",
              "name": "Weather",
              "icon": "🌤",
              "category": "apps",
              "fields": [field.as_dict() for field in WEATHER_FIELDS],
          },
          {
              "key": "markets",
              "name": "Markets",
              "icon": "📈",
              "category": "apps",
              "fields": [field.as_dict() for field in (*STOCK_FIELDS, *CRYPTO_FIELDS)],
          },
          {
              "key": "sports",
              "name": "Sports",
              "icon": "🏒",
              "category": "apps",
              "fields": [field.as_dict() for field in SPORTS_FIELDS],
          },
          {
              "key": "transit",
              "name": "Transit",
              "icon": "🚇",
              "category": "apps",
              "fields": [field.as_dict() for field in METRO_FIELDS],
          },
          {
              "key": "time",
              "name": "Time",
              "icon": "⏳",
              "category": "apps",
              "fields": [
                  field.as_dict()
                  for field in (*COUNTDOWN_FIELDS, *WORLD_CLOCK_FIELDS)
              ],
          },
          {
              "key": "animations",
              "name": "Animations",
              "icon": "🎨",
              "category": "apps",
              "fields": [field.as_dict() for field in ANIMATION_FIELDS],
          },
      ]
      
      
      DEFAULT_SETTINGS: dict[str, Any] = {
          "row_counts": "",
          "default_drum": "",
          "rows": 0,
          "cols": 0,
          "ui_scale": 100,
          "timezone": "",
          "units": "auto",
          "page_delay": 5,
          "weather_entity": "",
          "zip_code": "",
          "weather_api_key": "",
          "stocks_list": "MSFT,GOOG,NVDA",
          "crypto_list": "bitcoin,ethereum,solana",
          "sports_teams": "BOS,DAL",
          "metro_stop": "place-bbsta",
          "metro_route": "Orange",
          "mbta_api_key": "",
          "countdown_event": "NEW YEAR",
          "countdown_target": "2027-01-01T00:00:00",
          "world_clock_zones": "US/Eastern,US/Pacific,Europe/London",
          "clock_format": "12h",
          "anim_effect": "rainbow",
          "anim_style": "ltr",
          "anim_speed": "0.4",
          "anim_text": "SPLIT  FLAP  DISPLAY",
      }
      
      # Fill in any default declared on a field but missing above.
      for _group in SETTINGS_GROUPS:
          for _field in _group["fields"]:
              if _field.get("default") not in (None, ""):
                  DEFAULT_SETTINGS.setdefault(_field["key"], _field["default"])
      
      
      SETTINGS_KEYS = frozenset(DEFAULT_SETTINGS)
      
      
      def settings_for_ui(settings: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
          """Return a merged, JSON-safe settings dictionary for the panel."""
      
          merged = dict(DEFAULT_SETTINGS)
          merged.update(
              {key: value for key, value in settings.items() if key in SETTINGS_KEYS}
          )
          return merged
```

```
          async def _pages_for_cycle(self) -> list[Page]:
              if self.mode == "playlist":
                  return list(self.playlist)
      
              if self.mode != "app" or not self.active_app:
                  return []
      
              provider = APP_PROVIDERS.get(self.active_app)
              if provider is None:
                  return [Page(self.lines("APP NOT FOUND", self.active_app, ""))]
      
              app = APP_DEFS_BY_KEY.get(self.active_app)
              if app is not None and not self._app_available(app)[0]:
                  _LOGGER.warning(
                      "Stopping %s: it no longer fits the display layout",
                      self.active_app,
                  )
                  self.mode = "idle"
                  self.active_app = None
                  return []
      
              try:
                  result = await provider(self, datetime.now(self.tz))
              except Exception as err:  # noqa: BLE001 - show an error page
                  _LOGGER.exception("App %s failed", self.active_app)
                  return [
                      Page(

                          delay=10.0,

              if result is None:

              if isinstance(result, Page):

          async def async_cached(
              self,
              key: str,
              ttl: float,
              factory: Callable[[], Awaitable[Any]],
          ) -> Any:
              now = time.monotonic()
              cached = self._cache.get(key)
              if cached is not None and now - cached[0] < ttl:
                  return cached[1]
      
              lock = self._cache_locks.setdefault(key, asyncio.Lock())
              async with lock:
                  cached = self._cache.get(key)
                  if cached is not None and time.monotonic() - cached[0] < ttl:
                      return cached[1]
                  value = await factory()
                  self._cache[key] = (time.monotonic(), value)
                  return value

                  params=params,
                  headers=headers,
                  timeout=self.http_timeout,
              ) as response:
                  response.raise_for_status()
                  return await response.json(content_type=None)

        _loadDrumToEditor(name) {
          if (!name) return;
          const drum = this._savedDrum(name);
          if (!this._validDrum(drum)) {
            this._toast(this._t("drum_length_error"), "warn");
            return;
          }
          const editor = this.shadowRoot.getElementById("drumEditor");
          const nameNode = this.shadowRoot.getElementById("drumName");
          if (editor) editor.value = drum;
          // Pre-fill the name so an edited drum saves over itself by default.
          if (nameNode) nameNode.value = name;
          this._updateDrumEditorCharCount();
          this._toast(formatMessage(this._t("drum_loaded"), { name }));
        }
      
        _openAppSettings(key) {
          const apps = (this._engine() && this._engine().apps) || [];
          const app = apps.find((item) => item.key === key);
          if (!app) return;
          this._modalApp = key;
          const settings = (this._engine() && this._engine().settings) || {};
          const fields = app.fields || [];
          this.shadowRoot.getElementById("modalTitle").textContent = formatMessage(
            this._t("app_settings_named"),
            { name: this._appName(key) }
          );
          this.shadowRoot.getElementById("modalFields").innerHTML = fields.length
            ? fields.map((field) => this._fieldHtml(field, settings[field.key])).join("")
            : `<p class="muted">${escapeHtml(this._t("app_no_options"))}</p>`;
          const saveBtn = this.shadowRoot.querySelector('[data-action="save-app-settings"]');
          if (saveBtn) saveBtn.classList.remove("hidden");
          this.shadowRoot.getElementById("modal").classList.remove("hidden");
        }
      
        _openAppMode(key) {
          const apps = (this._engine() && this._engine().apps) || [];
          const app = apps.find((item) => item.key === key);
          if (!app) return;
          const modes = Array.isArray(app.modes) ? app.modes : [];
          if (!modes.length) {
            // No variants: launch the app directly.
            this._startApp(key);
            return;
          }
          this._modalApp = key;
          this.shadowRoot.getElementById("modalTitle").textContent = formatMessage(
            this._t("app_mode_named"),
            { name: this._appName(key) }
          );
          this.shadowRoot.getElementById("modalFields").innerHTML = modes
            .map(
              (mode) =>
                `<button class="btn secondary" data-action="start-app-mode" data-app="${escapeAttr(
                  key
                )}" data-mode="${escapeAttr(mode)}">${escapeHtml(
                  this._appModeLabel(key, mode)
                )}</button>`
            )
            .join("");
          const saveBtn = this.shadowRoot.querySelector('[data-action="save-app-settings"]');
          if (saveBtn) saveBtn.classList.add("hidden");
          this.shadowRoot.getElementById("modal").classList.remove("hidden");
        }
      
        async _startApp(key) {
          const apps = (this._engine() && this._engine().apps) || [];
          const app = apps.find((item) => item.key === key);
          if (app && app.available === false) {
            const reason =
              this._appRequirement(app, this._board()) || this._t("display_too_small");
            this._toast(`${this._appName(key)}: ${reason}`, "warn");
            return;
          }
          await this._send("start_app", { app: key });
        }
      
        async _startAppMode(app, mode) {
          const apps = (this._engine() && this._engine().apps) || [];
          const found = apps.find((item) => item.key === app);
          if (found && found.available === false) {
            const reason =
              this._appRequirement(found, this._board()) || this._t("display_too_small");
            this._toast(`${this._appName(app)}: ${reason}`, "warn");
            return;
          }
          await this._send("start_app", { app, mode });
          this._closeModal();
        }
```

```
text: |
    #!/bin/bash
    # install.sh — Set up Splitflap OS on a Raspberry Pi (Bookworm / Trixie)
    # Run as root from the repo directory: sudo bash setup/install.sh
    set -e
    SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
    REPO_DIR="$(dirname "$SCRIPT_DIR")"
    VENV_DIR="$REPO_DIR/venv"
    echo "=== Splitflap OS Installer ==="
    echo " Installing from: $REPO_DIR"
    echo ""
    # Check root
    if [ "$EUID" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "ERROR: Please run as root (sudo bash setup/install.sh)"
    exit 1
    fi
    # Install system packages
    echo "[1/4] Installing system packages..."
    apt-get update -qq
    apt-get install -y python3-pip python3-venv network-manager libopenblas0
    # Ensure NetworkManager manages WiFi
    echo "[2/4] Configuring NetworkManager..."
    if ! systemctl is-active --quiet NetworkManager; then
    systemctl enable NetworkManager
    systemctl start NetworkManager
    fi
    # Create venv and install Python dependencies
    # Using a venv avoids PEP 668 conflicts on Bookworm/Trixie and keeps
    # dependencies isolated from the system Python.
    # --prefer-binary uses pre-built wheels — much faster on Pi Zero W (ARMv6).
    echo "[3/4] Installing Python dependencies..."
    if [ ! -d "$VENV_DIR" ]; then
    echo " Creating virtual environment..."
    python3 -m venv "$VENV_DIR"
    fi
    echo " Installing packages (this may take a while on Pi Zero W)..."
    "$VENV_DIR/bin/pip" install --prefer-binary -r "$REPO_DIR/server/requirements.txt"
    # Make scripts executable
    chmod +x "$REPO_DIR/setup/network-check.sh"
    # Install systemd services (preserve existing Environment= variables)
    echo "[4/4] Setting up systemd services..."
    install_service() {
    local src="$1"
    local dest="$2"
    local tmp=$(mktemp)
    sed "s|/opt/splitflap-os|$REPO_DIR|g" "$src" > "$tmp"
    # Preserve existing Environment= lines if service already installed
    if [ -f "$dest" ]; then
    while IFS= read -r line; do
    if [[ "$line" == Environment=* ]]; then
    key="${line%%=*}=${line#*=}"
    key="${line%%=*}"
    # Replace matching Environment= line with existing value
    sed -i "s|^${key}=.*|${line}|" "$tmp"
    fi
    done < "$dest"
    fi
    mv "$tmp" "$dest"
    }
    install_service "$REPO_DIR/setup/splitflap-network.service" /etc/systemd/system/splitflap-network.service
    install_service "$REPO_DIR/setup/splitflap.service" /etc/systemd/system/splitflap.service
    systemctl daemon-reload
    systemctl enable splitflap-network.service
    systemctl enable splitflap.service
    systemctl restart splitflap-network.service
```
