> _Reasoning_
> Registry defaults currently only app defaults; global defaults added by engine/loader combination. Better registry should include global defaults and display group so engine has one source. But loader importing settings creates settings→apps.common only, no cycle (loader imports .common and ..settings). apps/__init__ imports loader; settings imports apps.common. When importing apps.loader, it imports ..settings which imports apps.common; apps package __init__ is executing… potential circular: `custom_components.splitflap_os.apps.__init__` starts, imports `.loader`, loader does `from ..settings import ...`, settings does `from .apps.common import SettingField` → importing `custom_components.splitflap_os.apps` (already in sys.modules, partially initialized) then `.common` submodule import works. Probably fine, but safer: don't import settings in loader; pass global defaults/group into load_apps as args. Engine composes. But registry settings_for_ui needs all defaults. Let loader accept `global_defaults` and `display_group` params optional:

> ```
> def load_apps(apps_dir, *, global_defaults=None, display_group=None)

> Then defaults = dict(global_defaults or {}); update app fields. groups = [display_group] + app groups if provided.
> That keeps loader pure. Update loader accordingly.

{
  "path": "custom_components/splitflap_os/apps/countdown/app.py",
  "instructions": "Create the countdown app module.",
  "content": "\"\"\"Countdown app.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom datetime import datetime\n\nfrom ...models import Page\n\n\ndef _parse_target(ctx) -> datetime | None:\n    raw = str(ctx.get_setting(\"countdown_target\", \"\")).strip()\n    if not raw:\n        return None\n    try:\n        target = datetime.fromisoformat(raw)\n    except ValueError:\n        return None\n    if target.tzinfo is None:\n        target = target.replace(tzinfo=ctx.tz)\n    return target\n\n\nasync def fetch(ctx, now: datetime) -> list[Page]:\n    target = _parse_target(ctx)\n    event = str(ctx.get_setting(\"countdown_event\", \"COUNTDOWN\")).strip().upper()\n    if target is None:\n        return [Page(ctx.lines(event[: ctx.cols], \"SET TARGET\", \"IN SETTINGS\"))]\n\n    remaining = target - now.astimezone(ctx.tz)\n    total = int(remaining.total_seconds())\n    if total <= 0:\n        return [Page(ctx.lines(event[: ctx.cols], \"HAS PASSED\", \"\"))]\n\n    days, rem = divmod(total, 86_400)\n    hours, rem = divmod(rem, 3_600)\n    minutes, seconds = divmod(rem, 60)\n    return [\n        Page(\n            ctx.lines(\n                event[: ctx.cols],\n                f\"{days}D {hours:02d}H {minutes:02d}M\",\n                f\"{seconds:02d} SECONDS\",\n            ),\n            delay=1.0,\n        )\n    ]\n"
}

{
  "path": "custom_components/splitflap_os/apps/world_clock/app.py",
  "instructions": "Create the world clock app module.",
  "content": "\"\"\"World clock app.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom zoneinfo import ZoneInfo, ZoneInfoNotFoundError\n\nfrom ...models import Page\nfrom ..common import split_csv\n\n\ndef _time_text(dt: datetime, ctx) -> str:\n    pattern = str(ctx.get_setting(\"clock_format\", \"12h\")).lower()\n    if pattern in {\"24\", \"24h\"}:\n        return dt.strftime(\"%H:%M\")\n    return dt.strftime(\"%I:%M %p\").lstrip(\"0\")\n\n\ndef _zone_label(zone: str) -> str:\n    tail = zone.rsplit(\"/\", 1)[-1].replace(\"_\", \" \")\n    return tail.upper()\n\n\nasync def fetch(ctx, now: datetime) -> list[Page]:\n    zones = split_csv(ctx.get_setting(\"world_clock_zones\"))\n    if not zones:\n        zones = [\"UTC\"]\n\n    rows, cols = ctx.board\n    lines: list[str] = []\n    for zone_name in zones[:12]:\n        try:\n            dt = now.astimezone(ZoneInfo(zone_name))\n        except (ZoneInfoNotFoundError, ValueError):\n            lines.append(f\"BAD ZONE {zone_name}\"[:cols].center(cols))\n            continue\n        label = _zone_label(zone_name)[: max(1, cols - 6)]\n        lines.append(f\"{label} {_time_text(dt, ctx)}\"[:cols].center(cols))\n\n    pages: list[Page] = []\n    for start in range(0, len(lines), rows):\n        chunk = lines[start : start + rows]\n        while len(chunk) < rows:\n            chunk.append(\" \" * cols)\n        pages.append(Page(\"\\n\".join(chunk), delay=1.0))\n    return pages or [Page(ctx.lines(\"WORLD CLOCK\", \"NO ZONES\", \"\"))]\n"
}

  "content": "\"\"\"Weather app.\n\nHome Assistant weather entities are the primary source.  An OpenWeatherMap\nfallback is available for installations that do not have a weather entity.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom typing import Any\n\nfrom ...models import Page\nfrom ..common import condition_label\n\n_LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\ndef _source_unit(attrs: dict[str, Any]) -> str:\n    unit = str(attrs.get(\"temperature_unit\") or \"°C\")\n    return \"F\" if \"F\" in unit.upper() else \"C\"\n\n\ndef _format_temp(ctx, value: Any, source_unit: str) -> str:\n    try:\n        number = float(value)\n    except (TypeError, ValueError):\n        return \"--\"\n\n    target = ctx.unit_system\n    if target == \"imperial\" and source_unit == \"C\":\n        number = number * 9 / 5 + 32\n        unit = \"F\"\n    elif target == \"metric\" and source_unit == \"F\":\n        number = (number - 32) * 5 / 9\n        unit = \"C\"\n    else:\n        unit = source_unit\n    return f\"{round(number)}{unit}\"\n\n\nasync def _fetch_forecast(ctx, entity_id: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:\n    try:\n        response = await ctx.hass.services.async_call(\n            \"weather\",\n            \"get_forecasts\",\n            {\"entity_id\": entity_id, \"type\": \"daily\"},\n            blocking=True,\n            return_response=True,\n        )\n    except Exception as err:  # noqa: BLE001 - not every weather entity supports it\n        _LOGGER.debug(\"Weather forecast unavailable for %s: %s\", entity_id, err)\n        return []\n\n    if not isinstance(response, dict):\n        return []\n    entry = response.get(entity_id)\n    if not isinstance(entry, dict):\n        return []\n    forecast = entry.get(\"forecast\")\n    return forecast if isinstance(forecast, list) else []\n\n\nasync def _ha_weather(ctx) -> dict[str, Any] | None:\n    entity_id = str(ctx.get_setting(\"weather_entity\", \"\")).strip()\n    if not entity_id:\n        return None\n    state = ctx.hass.states.get(entity_id)\n    if state is None:\n        return None\n\n    attrs = dict(state.attributes)\n    forecast = await _fetch_forecast(ctx, entity_id)\n    return {\n        \"source\": \"ha\",\n        \"name\": state.name or entity_id,\n        \"condition\": state.state,\n        \"attrs\": attrs,\n        \"forecast\": forecast,\n        \"unit\": _source_unit(attrs),\n    }\n\n\nasync def _openweather(ctx) -> dict[str, Any] | None:\n    api_key = str(ctx.get_setting(\"weather_api_key\", \"\")).strip()\n    zip_code = str(ctx.get_setting(\"zip_code\", \"\")).strip()\n    if not api_key or not zip_code:\n        return None\n\n    units = \"imperial\" if ctx.unit_system == \"imperial\" else \"metric\"\n    current = await ctx.http_json(\n        \"https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather\",\n        params={\"zip\": zip_code, \"appid\": api_key, \"units\": units},\n    )\n    if not isinstance(current, dict):\n        return None\n\n    main = current.get(\"main\") or {}\n    weather = (current.get(\"weather\") or [{}])[0]\n    forecast_data = await ctx.http_json(\n        \"https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/forecast\",\n        params={\"zip\": zip_code, \"appid\": api_key, \"units\": units},\n    )\n    high = low = None\n    if isinstance(forecast_data, dict):\n        values = [\n            (item.get(\"main\") or {}).get(\"temp\")\n            for item in forecast_data.get(\"list\", [])\n            if isinstance(item, dict)\n        ]\n        values = [value for value in values if isinstance(value, (int, float))]\n        if values:\n            high, low = max(values), min(values)\n\n    return {\n        \"source\": \"openweather\",\n        \"name\": str(current.get(\"name\") or zip_code),\n        \"condition\": weather.get(\"main\", \"UNKNOWN\"),\n        \"attrs\": {\n            \"temperature\": main.get(\"temp\"),\n            \"apparent_temperature\": main.get(\"feels_like\"),\n            \"humidity\": main.get(\"humidity\"),\n            \"wind_speed\": (current.get(\"wind\") or {}).get(\"speed\"),\n            \"temperature_unit\": \"F\" if units == \"imperial\" else \"C\",\n        },\n        \"forecast\": [{\"temperature\": high, \"templow\": low}] if high is not None else [],\n        \"unit\": \"F\" if units == \"imperial\" else \"C\",\n    }\n\n\nasync def _snapshot(ctx) -> dict[str, Any] | None:\n    data = await _ha_weather(ctx)\n    if data is None:\n        data = await _openweather(ctx)\n    return data\n\n\nasync def fetch(ctx, now: datetime) -> list[Page]:\n    try:\n        data = await ctx.async_cached(\n            \"weather\", 15 * 60, lambda: _snapshot(ctx)\n        )\n    except Exception as err:  # noqa: BLE001 - show an error page, never crash the loop\n        _LOGGER.warning(\"Weather fetch failed: %s\", err)\n        data = None\n\n    if not data:\n        return [\n            Page(\n                ctx.lines(\n                    \"WEATHER\",\n                    \"SET ENTITY\",\n                    \"IN SETTINGS\",\n                ),\n                delay=5.0,\n            )\n        ]\n\n    attrs = data.get(\"attrs\") or {}\n    unit = data.get(\"unit\") or \"C\"\n    name = str(data.get(\"name\") or \"WEATHER\").upper()\n    condition = condition_label(data.get(\"condition\"))\n    temp = _format_temp(ctx, attrs.get(\"temperature\"), unit)\n    feels = _format_temp(ctx, attrs.get(\"apparent_temperature\"), unit)\n    high = low = None\n    forecast = data.get(\"forecast\") or []\n    if forecast and isinstance(forecast[0], dict):\n        high = _format_temp(ctx, forecast[0].get(\"temperature\"), unit)\n        low = _format_temp(ctx, forecast[0].get(\"templow\"), unit)\n\n    humidity = attrs.get(\"humidity\")\n    wind = attrs.get(\"wind_speed\")\n    extra: list[str] = []\n    if high != \"--\" and low != \"--\":\n        extra.append(f\"H:{high} L:{low}\")\n    if feels != \"--\":\n        extra.append(f\"FEELS {feels}\")\n    if humidity is not None:\n        try:\n            extra.append(f\"HUM {round(float(humidity))}%\")\n        except (TypeError, ValueError):\n            pass\n    if wind is not None:\n        try:\n            extra.append(f\"WIND {round(float(wind))}\")\n        except (TypeError, ValueError):\n            pass\n\n    lines = [name, f\"{temp} {condition}\"]\n    lines.extend(extra)\n    return [Page(ctx.lines(*lines), delay=5.0)]\n"
}

compact_number, signed_percent, split_csv\n\n_LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\nasync def _yahoo_quote(ctx, symbol: str) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    url = (\n        \"https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/\"\n        f\"{symbol}?range=1d&interval=5m\"\n    )\n    data = await ctx.http_json(url, headers={\"User-Agent\": \"Mozilla/5.0\"})\n    result = ((data or {}).get(\"chart\") or {}).get(\"result\") or []\n    if not result:\n        raise ValueError(f\"No quote for {symbol}\")\n    meta = result[0].get(\"meta\") or {}\n    price = meta.get(\"regularMarketPrice\")\n    previous = meta.get(\"chartPreviousClose\") or meta.get(\"previousClose\")\n    if price is None:\n        indicators = result[0].get(\"indicators\") or {}\n        quotes = indicators.get(\"quote\") or [{}]\n        closes = [v for v in (quotes[0].get(\"close\") or []) if v is not None]\n        if closes:\n            price = closes[-1]\n            previous = previous or closes[0]\n    if price is None:\n        raise ValueError(f\"No price for {symbol}\")\n    return {\n        \"symbol\": symbol.upper(),\n        \"price\": float(price),\n        \"previous\": float(previous) if previous is not None else None,\n        \"currency\": meta.get(\"currency\", \"USD\"),\n        \"name\": meta.get(\"shortName\") or symbol.upper(),\n    }\n\n\nasync def _stooq_quote(ctx, symbol: str) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    ticker = symbol.lower()\n    if \".\" not in ticker:\n        ticker = f\"{ticker}.us\"\n    url = f\"https://stooq.com/q/l/?s={ticker}&f=sd2t2ohlcv&h&e=csv\"\n    session = ctx.session\n    async with session.get(url, timeout=ctx.http_timeout) as response:\n        response.raise_for_status()\n        text = await response.text()\n    lines = [line for line in text.splitlines() if line.strip()]\n    if len(lines) < 2:\n        raise ValueError(f\"No Stooq quote for {symbol}\")\n    header = [part.strip() for part in lines[0].split(\",\")]\n    values = [part.strip() for part in lines[1].split(\",\")]\n    row = dict(zip(header, values))\n    close = float(row[\"Close\"])\n    open_price = float(row[\"Open\"]) if row.get(\"Open\") not in (None, \"\", \"N/A\") else None\n    return {\n        \"symbol\": symbol.upper(),\n        \"price\": close,\n        \"previous\": open_price,\n        \"currency\": \"USD\",\n        \"name\": symbol.upper(),\n    }\n\n\nasync def _quote(ctx, symbol: str) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    try:\n        return await _yahoo_quote(ctx, symbol)\n    except Exception as err:  # noqa: BLE001 - fall back to Stooq\n        _LOGGER.debug(\"Yahoo quote failed for %s: %s\", symbol, err)\n        return await _stooq_quote(ctx, symbol)\n\n\nasync def fetch(ctx, now: datetime) -> list[Page]:\n    symbols = split_csv(ctx.get_setting(\"stocks_list\"))[:8]\n    if not symbols:\n        return [Page(ctx.lines(\"STOCKS\", \"SET SYMBOLS\", \"IN SETTINGS\"))]\n\n    async def fetch_quotes() -> list[dict[str, Any]]:\n        results: list[dict[str, Any]] = []\n        for symbol in symbols:\n            try:\n                results.append(await _quote(ctx, symbol))\n            except Exception as err:  # noqa: BLE001 - keep the other symbols\n                _LOGGER.warning(\"Stock quote failed for %s: %s\", symbol, err)\n                results.append({\"symbol\": symbol.upper(), \"error\": True})\n        return results\n\n    try:\n        quotes = await ctx.async_cached(\"stocks\", 60, fetch_quotes)\n    except Exception as err:  # noqa: BLE001\n        _LOGGER.warning(\"Stock fetch failed: %s\", err)\n        return [Page(ctx.lines(\"STOCKS\", \"DATA ERROR\", \"CHECK NETWORK\"))]\n\n    pages: list[Page] = []\n    for quote in quotes:\n        if quote.get(\"error\"):\n            pages.append(Page(ctx.lines(quote[\"symbol\"], \"NO DATA\", \"\"), delay=4.0))\n            continue\n        price = compact_number(float(quote[\"price\"]), currency=quote.get(\"currency\", \"\"))\n        change_text = \"\"\n        previous = quote.get(\"previous\")\n        if previous:\n            change = (float(quote[\"price\"]) - float(previous)) / float(previous) * 100\n            change_text = signed_percent(change)\n        pages.append(\n            Page(\n                ctx.lines(\n                    quote.get(\"symbol\", \"?\"),\n                    price,\n                    change_text,\n                ),\n                delay=4.0,\n            )\n        )\n    return pages or [Page(ctx.lines(\"STOCKS\", \"NO DATA\", \"\"))]\n"
}

{
  "path": "custom_components/splitflap_os/apps/crypto/app.py",
  "instructions": "Create the crypto app module.",
  "content": "\"\"\"Crypto app.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom typing import Any\n\nfrom ...models import Page\nfrom ..common import compact_number, signed_percent, split_csv\n\n_LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\nasync def _crypto_quotes(ctx) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:\n    coins = split_csv(ctx.get_setting(\"crypto_list\"))[:8]\n    if not coins:\n        return []\n    data = await ctx.http_json(\n        \"https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/simple/price\",\n        params={\n            \"ids\": \",\".join(coins),\n            \"vs_currencies\": \"usd\",\n            \"include_24hr_change\": \"true\",\n        },\n        headers={\"User-Agent\": \"Split-Flap-OS/1.0\"},\n    )\n    results: list[dict[str, Any]] = []\n    for coin in coins:\n        item = (data or {}).get(coin) or {}\n        if not item:\n            results.append({\"id\": coin, \"error\": True})\n            continue\n        results.append(\n            {\n                \"id\": coin,\n                \"name\": coin.replace(\"-\", \" \").upper(),\n                \"price\": item.get(\"usd\"),\n                \"change\": item.get(\"usd_24h_change\"),\n            }\n        )\n    return results\n\n\nasync def fetch(ctx, now: datetime) -> list[Page]:\n    try:\n        quotes = await ctx.async_cached(\"crypto\", 60, lambda: _crypto_quotes(ctx))\n    except Exception as err:  # noqa: BLE001\n        _LOGGER.warning(\"Crypto fetch failed: %s\", err)\n        return [Page(ctx.lines(\"CRYPTO\", \"DATA ERROR\", \"CHECK NETWORK\"))]\n\n    if not quotes:\n        return [Page(ctx.lines(\"CRYPTO\", \"SET COINS\", \"IN SETTINGS\"))]\n\n    pages: list[Page] = []\n    for quote in quotes:\n        if quote.get(\"error\"):\n            pages.append(Page(ctx.lines(str(quote[\"id\"]).upper(), \"NO DATA\", \"\"), delay=4.0))\n            continue\n        price = quote.get(\"price\")\n        price_text = compact_number(float(price), currency=\"USD\") if price is not None else \"--\"\n        change = quote.get(\"change\")\n        change_text = signed_percent(float(change)) if change is not None else \"\"\n        pages.append(\n            Page(\n                ctx.lines(str(quote.get(\"name\", \"?\")).upper(), price_text, change_text),\n                delay=4.0,\n            )\n        )\n    return pages\n"
}

...models import Page\nfrom ..common import split_csv\n\n_LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\ndef _team_name(competitor: dict[str, Any]) -> str:\n    team = competitor.get(\"team\") or {}\n    return str(\n        team.get(\"abbreviation\")\n        or team.get(\"shortDisplayName\")\n        or team.get(\"displayName\")\n        or \"?\"\n    ).upper()\n\n\nasync def _scoreboard(ctx) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    return await ctx.http_json(\n        \"https://site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/hockey/nhl/scoreboard\",\n        headers={\"User-Agent\": \"Split-Flap-OS/1.0\"},\n    )\n\n\ndef _games(data: dict[str, Any], teams: list[str]) -> list[dict[str, str]]:\n    wanted = {team.upper() for team in teams}\n    results: list[dict[str, str]] = []\n\n    for event in (data or {}).get(\"events\", []):\n        competitions = event.get(\"competitions\") or []\n        if not competitions:\n            continue\n        competition = competitions[0]\n        competitors = competition.get(\"competitors\") or []\n        if len(competitors) < 2:\n            continue\n\n        parsed: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}\n        for competitor in competitors:\n            side = str(competitor.get(\"homeAway\") or \"\").lower()\n            parsed[side or \"other\"] = competitor\n        away = parsed.get(\"away\") or competitors[0]\n        home = parsed.get(\"home\") or competitors[1]\n        away_name = _team_name(away)\n        home_name = _team_name(home)\n\n        if wanted and away_name not in wanted and home_name not in wanted:\n            continue\n\n        status = (\n            ((competition.get(\"status\") or {}).get(\"type\") or {}).get(\"shortDetail\")\n            or \"SCHEDULED\"\n        )\n        results.append(\n            {\n                \"away\": away_name,\n                \"home\": home_name,\n                \"away_score\": str(away.get(\"score\") or \"-\"),\n                \"home_score\": str(home.get(\"score\") or \"-\"),\n                \"status\": str(status).upper(),\n            }\n        )\n    return results\n\n\nasync def fetch(ctx, now: datetime) -> list[Page]:\n    teams = split_csv(ctx.get_setting(\"sports_teams\"))\n    try:\n        data = await ctx.async_cached(\"sports\", 120, lambda: _scoreboard(ctx))\n    except Exception as err:  # noqa: BLE001\n        _LOGGER.warning(\"Sports fetch failed: %s\", err)\n        return [Page(ctx.lines(\"SPORTS\", \"DATA ERROR\", \"CHECK NETWORK\"))]\n\n    games = _games(data, teams)\n    if not games:\n        subject = teams[0].upper() if teams else \"GAMES\"\n        return [Page(ctx.lines(subject, \"NO GAME\", \"TODAY\"))]\n\n    pages: list[Page] = []\n    for game in games:\n        pages.append(\n            Page(\n                ctx.lines(\n                    f\"{game['away']} {game['away_score']}\",\n                    f\"{game['home']} {game['home_score']}\",\n                    game[\"status\"],\n                ),\n                delay=5.0,\n            )\n        )\n    return pages\n"
}

{
  "path": "custom_components/splitflap_os/apps/metro/app.py",
  "instructions": "Create the metro app module.",
  "content": "\"\"\"Transit app using the MBTA v3 API (no key required for light use).\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\nfrom typing import Any\n\nfrom ...models import Page\n\n_LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\ndef _parse_time(value: Any) -> datetime | None:\n    if not value:\n        return None\n    try:\n        parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(str(value).replace(\"Z\", \"+00:00\"))\n    except ValueError:\n        return None\n    if parsed.tzinfo is None:\n        parsed = parsed.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)\n    return parsed\n\n\nasync def _predictions(ctx) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:\n    stop = str(ctx.get_setting(\"metro_stop\", \"\")).strip()\n    route = str(ctx.get_setting(\"metro_route\", \"\")).strip()\n    if not stop:\n        return []\n\n    params: dict[str, Any] = {\n        \"filter[stop]\": stop,\n        \"sort\": \"time\",\n        \"page[limit]\": 4,\n    }\n    if route:\n        params[\"filter[route]\"] = route\n    api_key = str(ctx.get_setting(\"mbta_api_key\", \"\")).strip()\n    if api_key:\n        params[\"api_key\"] = api_key\n\n    data = await ctx.http_json(\n        \"https://api-v3.mbta.com/predictions\", params=params\n    )\n    return (data or {}).get(\"data\", [])  # type: ignore[union-attr]\n\n\nasync def fetch(ctx, now: datetime) -> list[Page]:\n    stop = str(ctx.get_setting(\"metro_stop\", \"\")).strip()\n    route = str(ctx.get_setting(\"metro_route\", \"\")).strip() or \"TRANSIT\"\n    if not stop:\n        return [Page(ctx.lines(route.upper(), \"SET STOP\", \"IN SETTINGS\"))]\n\n    try:\n        predictions = await ctx.async_cached(\n            \"metro\", 30, lambda: _predictions(ctx)\n        )\n    except Exception as err:  # noqa: BLE001\n        _LOGGER.warning(\"Metro fetch failed: %s\", err)\n        return [Page(ctx.lines(route.upper(), \"DATA ERROR\", \"CHECK NETWORK\"))]\n\n    if not predictions:\n        return [Page(ctx.lines(route.upper(), \"NO\", \"PREDICTIONS\"))]\n\n    pages: list[Page] = []\n    for prediction in predictions:\n        attrs = prediction.get(\"attributes\") or {}\n        when = _parse_time(attrs.get(\"arrival_time\") or attrs.get(\"departure_time\"))\n        if when is None:\n            continue\n        minutes = max(0, int((when - now.astimezone(timezone.utc)).total_seconds() // 60))\n        direction = \"OUT\" if attrs.get(\"direction_id\") == 1 else \"IN\"\n        pages.append(\n            Page(\n                ctx.lines(\n                    f\"{route.upper()} {direction}\",\n                    f\"{minutes} MIN\",\n                    when.astimezone(ctx.tz).strftime(\"%I:%M %p\").lstrip(\"0\"),\n                ),\n                delay=5.0,\n            )\n        )\n    return pages or [Page(ctx.lines(route.upper(), \"NO\", \"PREDICTIONS\"))]\n"
}

{
  "path": "custom_components/splitflap_os/apps/iss/app.py",
  "instructions": "Create the ISS app module.",
  "content": "\"\"\"ISS position app.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom typing import Any\n\nfrom ...models import Page\n\n_LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\nasync def _position(ctx) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    return await ctx.http_json(\n        \"https://api.wheretheiss.at/v1/satellites/25544\",\n        headers={\"User-Agent\": \"Split-Flap-OS/1.0\"},\n    )\n\n\nasync def fetch(ctx, now: datetime) -> list[Page]:\n    try:\n        data = await ctx.async_cached(\"iss\", 5, lambda: _position(ctx))\n    except Exception as err:  # noqa: BLE001\n        _LOGGER.warning(\"ISS fetch failed: %s\", err)\n        return [Page(ctx.lines(\"ISS\", \"DATA ERROR\", \"CHECK NETWORK\"))]\n\n    if not isinstance(data, dict):\n        return [Page(ctx.lines(\"ISS\", \"NO DATA\", \"\"))]\n\n    latitude = data.get(\"latitude\")\n    longitude = data.get(\"longitude\")\n    altitude = data.get(\"altitude\")\n    velocity = data.get(\"velocity\")\n\n    def _coord(value: Any, positive: str, negative: str) -> str:\n        try:\n            number = float(value)\n        except (TypeError, ValueError):\n            return \"--\"\n        return f\"{abs(number):.2f}{positive if number >= 0 else negative}\"\n\n    lines = [\n        \"ISS\",\n        f\"LAT {_coord(latitude, 'N', 'S')}\",\n        f\"LON {_coord(longitude, 'E', 'W')}\",\n    ]\n    if altitude is not None:\n        try:\n            lines.append(f\"ALT {round(float(altitude))} KM\")\n        except (TypeError, ValueError):\n            pass\n    if velocity is not None:\n        try:\n            lines.append(f\"VEL {round(float(velocity))} KMH\")\n        except (TypeError, ValueError):\n            pass\n    return [Page(ctx.lines(*lines), delay=5.0)]\n"
}

{
  "path": "custom_components/splitflap_os/apps/animations/app.py",
  "instructions": "Create the animations app module.",
  "content": "\"\"\"Colour animations, generated as complete raw frames.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport random\nfrom datetime import datetime\n\nfrom ...layout import COLOR_CODES\nfrom ...models import Page\nfrom ..common import as_float\n\n\ndef _rainbow(rows: int, cols: int) -> list[str]:\n    pages: list[str] = []\n    for offset in range(len(COLOR_CODES)):\n        board = \"\".join(\n            COLOR_CODES[(column + row + offset) % len(COLOR_CODES)]\n            for row in range(rows)\n            for column in range(cols)\n        )\n        pages.append(board)\n    return pages\n\n\ndef _sweep(rows: int, cols: int) -> list[str]:\n    pages: list[str] = []\n    steps = list(range(1, cols + 1)) + list(range(cols - 1, 0, -1))\n    for step in steps:\n        colour = COLOR_CODES[step % len(COLOR_CODES)]\n        board = \"\".join(\n            colour if column < step else \" \"\n            for _row in range(rows)\n            for column in range(cols)\n        )\n        pages.append(board)\n    return pages\n\n\ndef _checker(rows: int, cols: int) -> list[str]:\n    pages: list[str] = []\n    pairs = [\n        (\"r\", \"b\"),\n        (\"o\", \"p\"),\n        (\"y\", \"g\"),\n        (\"r\", \"w\"),\n        (\"g\", \"b\"),\n    ]\n    for first, second in pairs:\n        for flip in (0, 1):\n            board = \"\".join(\n                (first if (row + column + flip) % 2 == 0 else second)\n                for row in range(rows)\n                for column in range(cols)\n            )\n            pages.append(board)\n    return pages\n\n\ndef _twinkle(rows: int, cols: int, count: int = 12) -> list[str]:\n    palette = COLOR_CODES + \"     \"\n    return [\n        \"\".join(random.choice(palette) for _ in range(rows * cols))\n        for _ in range(count)\n    ]\n\n\nasync def fetch(ctx, now: datetime) -> list[Page]:\n    rows, cols = ctx.board\n    effect = str(ctx.get_setting(\"anim_effect\", \"rainbow\")).lower()\n    style = str(ctx.get_setting(\"anim_style\", \"ltr\"))\n    speed = max(0.1, as_float(ctx.get_setting(\"anim_speed\", \"0.4\"), 0.4))\n\n    if effect in {\"sweep\", \"wave\"}:\n        frames = _sweep(rows, cols)\n    elif effect in {\"checker\", \"checkerboard\"}:\n        frames = _checker(rows, cols)\n    elif effect in {\"twinkle\", \"sparkle\"}:\n        frames = _twinkle(rows, cols)\n    else:\n        frames = _rainbow(rows, cols)\n\n    return [\n        Page(\n            frame,\n            raw=True,\n            resend=True,\n            delay=speed,\n            style=style,\n        )\n        for frame in frames\n    ]\n"
}

"""Pure-Python tests for the board layout helpers.

Run with ``python3 tests/test_layout.py`` (Home Assistant is not required).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys
import unittest

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
COMPONENT_DIR = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(HERE), "custom_components", "splitflap_os")
sys.path.insert(0, COMPONENT_DIR)

import layout  # noqa: E402  (path is prepared above)


class NormalizeTextTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_uppercases_and_maps_quote(self) -> None:
        # The physical double-quote flap is addressed as lower-case ``q`` by
        # the firmware (see Adam's reference implementation).
        self.assertEqual(layout.normalize_text('hello "world"'), "HELLO qWORLDq")

    def test_maps_colour_emoji(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(layout.normalize_text("\U0001f7e5\U0001f7e6X"), "rbX")
        self.assertEqual(layout.normalize_text("\U0001fa75\U0001fa77"), "cm")

    def test_raw_keeps_case(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(layout.normalize_text("aBc", raw=True), "aBc")

    def test_none_becomes_blank(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(layout.normalize_text(None), "")


class AutoBoardTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_known_sizes(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(layout.auto_board(45), (3, 15))
        self.assertEqual(layout.auto_board(64), (4, 16))

    def test_rows_override(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(layout.auto_board(45, rows=5), (5, 9))

    def test_columns_override(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(layout.auto_board(45, cols=20), (3, 20))

    def test_both_overrides(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(layout.auto_board(45, rows=2, cols=8), (2, 8))

    def test_unknown_count_is_wide(self) -> None:
        rows, cols = layout.auto_board(41)
        self.assertEqual(rows, 3)
        self.assertEqual(cols, 14)

    def test_small_counts_are_one_row(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(layout.auto_board(1), (1, 1))
        self.assertEqual(layout.auto_board(7), (1, 7))
        self.assertEqual(layout.auto_board(12), (1, 12))

    def test_zero_modules_still_has_a_board(self) -> None:

"""Pure-Python tests for position-map normalization.

Run with ``python3 tests/test_positions.py`` (Home Assistant is not required).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys
import unittest

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
COMPONENT_DIR = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(HERE), "custom_components", "splitflap_os")
sys.path.insert(0, COMPONENT_DIR)

import positions  # noqa: E402  (path is prepared above)


class NormalizePositionMapTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_unset_sentinel_is_omitted(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(
            positions.normalize_position_map("0=2832,1=65535,2=0"),
            {"0": 2832, "2": 0},
        )

    def test_all_unset_returns_none(self) -> None:
        self.assertIsNone(positions.normalize_position_map("0=65535,1=65535"))

    def test_json_string(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(
            positions.normalize_position_map('{"0": 2832, "1": 65535}'),
            {"0": 2832},
        )

    def test_dict_values_are_coerced(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(
            positions.normalize_position_map({"0": "2832", "1": 65535}),
            {"0": 2832},
        )

      "newString": "        if self.mode == \"app\" and self.active_app and self.registry:\n            app = self.registry.app(self.active_app)\n            if app is not None:\n                return float(app.default_delay)\n        try:\n            return float(self.settings.get(\"page_delay\", 5.0) or 5.0)\n        except (TypeError, ValueError):\n            return 5.0\n\n    async def _sleep(self, seconds: float) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Wait for a page, interrupting the wait for queued notifications.\n\n        ``_stop_event`` still stops the loop immediately; a notification sets\n        ``_wake_event`` so the remaining delay is paused, the message shown,\n        and the wait then resumed for the time that was left.\n        \"\"\"\n\n        if seconds <= 0:\n            await asyncio.sleep(0)\n            return\n\n        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()\n        deadline = loop.time() + seconds\n        while True:\n            remaining = deadline - loop.time()\n            if remaining <= 0:\n                return\n            stop_wait = asyncio.create_task(self._stop_event.wait())\n            wake_wait = asyncio.create_task(self._wake_event.wait())\n            _, pending = await asyncio.wait(\n                {stop_wait, wake_wait},\n                timeout=remaining,\n                return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED,\n            )\n            for task in pending:\n                task.cancel()\n            if pending:\n                await asyncio.gather(*pending, return_exceptions=True)\n            if self._stop_event.is_set():\n                return\n            if self._wake_event.is_set():\n                self._wake_event.clear()\n                await self._drain_notifications()\n\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    # Notifications\n    # ------------------------------------------------------------------\n    async def _show_notification(self, item: dict[str, Any]) -> None:\n        rows, cols = self.board\n        lines, board = compose_board(item[\"text\"], rows, cols)\n        page = Page(text=item[\"text\"], style=item[\"style\"])\n        await self._publish_board(lines, board, item[\"style\"], page)\n        self._last_style = item[\"style\"]\n        self._last_speed = None\n        self._last_text = item[\"text\"]\n\n    async def _drain_notifications(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Show queued messages, then let the caller continue where it was.\"\"\"\n\n        while self._notifications and self.mode != \"idle\":\n            item = self._notifications.pop(0)\n            try:\n                await self._show_notification(item)\n            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - a bad message must not kill the loop\n                _LOGGER.exception(\"Could not display Split-Flap OS notification\")\n                continue\n            try:\n                await asyncio.wait_for(\n                    self._stop_event.wait(), timeout=item[\"seconds\"]\n                )\n            except asyncio.TimeoutError:\n                pass\n            if self._stop_event.is_set():\n                return\n\n    def _start_idle_notifications(self) -> None:\n        if self._idle_notify_task and not self._idle_notify_task.done():\n            return\n        self._idle_notify_task = self.hass.async_create_task(\n            self._run_idle_notifications()\n        )\n\n    async def _run_idle_notifications(self) -> None:\n        state = self._capture_display_state()\n        try:\n            while self._notifications and self.mode == \"idle\":\n                item = self._notifications.pop(0)\n                await self._show_notification(item)\n                try:\n                    await asyncio.wait_for(\n                        self._stop_event.wait(), timeout=item[\"seconds\"]\n                    )\n                except asyncio.TimeoutError:\n                    pass\n        except asyncio.CancelledError:\n            pass\n        finally:\n            if self._idle_notify_task is asyncio.current_task():\n                self._idle_notify_task = None\n            if self.mode == \"idle\":\n                await self._restore_display_state(state)\n\n    async def _cancel_idle_notifications(self) -> None:\n        task = self._idle_notify_task\n        if task is None:\n            return\n        self._idle_notify_task = None\n        if task is asyncio.current_task():\n            return\n        task.cancel()\n        try:\n            await task\n        except (asyncio.CancelledError, Exception):  # noqa: BLE001\n            pass\n\n    def _capture_display_state(self) -> dict[str, Any]:\n        return {\n            \"lines\": list(self._last_lines),\n            \"board\": self._last_board,\n            \"style\": self._last_style,\n            \"speed\": self._last_speed,\n            \"text\": self._last_text,\n            \"page\": self._current_page,\n            \"index\": self._current_page_index,\n            \"count\": self._current_page_count,\n        }\n\n    async def _restore_display_state(self, state: dict[str, Any]) -> None:\n        rows, cols = self.board\n        lines = state.get(\"lines\") or [\" \" * cols for _ in range(rows)]\n        board = state.get(\"board\") or (\" \" * (rows * cols))\n        style = state.get(\"style\") or \"ltr\"\n        page = Page(\n            text=state.get(\"text\") or \"\",\n            style=style,\n            speed=state.get(\"speed\"),\n        )\n        try:\n            await self._publish_board(lines, board, style, page)\n        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - restoring is best effort\n            _LOGGER.exception(\"Could not restore the display after a notification\")\n        self._last_lines = list(state.get(\"lines\") or [])\n        self._last_board = state.get(\"board\") or \"\"\n        self._last_style = state.get(\"style\")\n        self._last_speed = state.get(\"speed\")\n        self._last_text = state.get(\"text\") or \"\"\n        self._current_page = state.get(\"page\")\n        self._current_page_index = int(state.get(\"index\") or 0)\n        self._current_page_count = int(state.get(\"count\") or 0)\n        self._notify()",

      | Sports | 3 × 8 |
      | Metro | 3 × 10 |
      | Countdown | 3 × 12 |
      | World Clock | 1 × 10 |
      | ISS | 3 × 10 |
      
      Unsupported app cards are disabled and show the requirement. Starting one from
      the panel or a service returns an error. If a running app becomes unsupported
      because the layout changed, the engine stops it.
      
      ## MQTT contract
      
      The integration expects the master's retained status payload to look like this
      (abridged):
      
      ```json
      {
        "state": "online",
        "text": "HELLO",
        "version": "1.1.0.0",
        "bus_compat": 1,
        "mqtt_compat": 1,
        "compat": 1,
        "modules_count": 45,
        "modules": [
          {
            "id": 1,
            "state": "online",
            "online": true,
            "flap": "H",
            "total_steps": 4096,
            "home_offset": 2832,
            "current_step": 3616,
            "flap_list": " ABC...",
            "map_of_positions": {"0": 2832, "1": 2896},
            "fw_version": "1.0.1",
            "fw_bus_compat": 1,
            "fw_bus_compatible": true,
            "fw_compat": 1,
            "fw_compatible": true
          }
        ]
      }
      ```
      
      `version`/`bus_compat`/`mqtt_compat` are the master's own version contract;
      `compat` remains an alias for `mqtt_compat` for older integration builds. The
      per-module `fw_version`/`fw_bus_compat` come from the slave's `m<id>s` reply;
      `fw_bus_compatible` is omitted when the module does not report a version, and
      `fw_compat`/`fw_compatible` remain aliases for the bus values.
      
      Display commands are sent as an ordered array so the array order doubles as the
      animation order:
      
      ```json
      {"modules": [{"id": 1, "char": "H"}, {"id": 2, "char": "I"}]}
      ```
      
      Calibration commands use `{"module": 1, "action": "goto", "index": 5}` and the
      master translates them to the slave protocol.
      
      Position-map entries with the slave's `0xFFFF` sentinel are treated as unset:
      they are omitted from snapshots, never shown as tuned in the character map,
      and the integration falls back to the estimated flap position. Negative and
      out-of-range entries are ignored in the same way. An explicit `positions`
      object sent to the `calibrate` service may still contain `65535` to clear a
      single entry on the slave.
      
      ## Versions and module firmware
      
      All three parts of the system (slave firmware, ESP32 master, this integration)
      use two independent **compatibility axes** because two different peers talk to
      each other:
      
      | Axis | Peer contract | Carried by |
      | --- | --- | --- |
      | **BUS_COMPAT** | RS485 application protocol and the OTA/bootloader entry contract | slave + master |
      | **MQTT_COMPAT** | MQTT status/command JSON schema | master + Home Assistant |
      
      The master bridges the two, so it carries both numbers. Each repository also
      has its own release inside those generations, and the published version is
      composed from the numbers that apply to it:
      
      ```
      slave    <bus>.<release>              1.0.1      bus 1, release 0.1
      master   <bus>.<mqtt>.<release>       1.1.0.0    bus 1, mqtt 1, release 0.0
      HA       <mqtt>.<release>             1.1.0      mqtt 1, release 0.8
      ```
      
      | Where | Version | Compatibility | Read from |
      | --- | --- | --- | --- |
      | Home Assistant integration | `1.1.0` | MQTT `1` | panel header, connection info, WebSocket `version`/`mqtt_compat` |
      | ESP32 master | `1.1.0.0` | bus `1`, MQTT `1` | status `version`/`bus_compat`/`mqtt_compat`, connection info |
      | Slave application | `1.0.1` | bus `1` | panel module inspector, firmware card, `m<id>v`, UPDI dump |
      
      The integration compares the master's `mqtt_compat` with `MQTT_COMPAT` in
      `const.py`. A mismatch shows a warning banner, but it never blocks display
      traffic, OTA cancellation or a module reset. If the master predates the version
      protocol, the panel says the version is unknown rather than assuming it is
      compatible. The bus generation is shown for diagnostics; the slave <-> master

      ## 11. Verze a firmware modulů
      
      Všechny tři části systému (firmware modulů, ESP32 master a tato integrace)
      používají dvě nezávislé **osy kompatibility**, protože spolu mluví dva různé
      páry partnerů:
      
      | Osa | Kontrakt | Kdo ji nese |
      | --- | --- | --- |
      | **BUS_COMPAT** | RS485 aplikační protokol a kontrakt vstupu do OTA/bootloaderu | modul + master |
      | **MQTT_COMPAT** | JSON schéma MQTT statusu a příkazů | master + Home Assistant |
      
      Master obě strany propojuje, takže nese obě čísla. Každý repozitář má navíc
      vlastní vydání v rámci těchto generací a zobrazovaná verze se skládá z čísel,
      která se na něj vztahují:
      
      ```
      modul    <bus>.<vydání>               1.0.1      bus 1, vydání 0.1
      master   <bus>.<mqtt>.<vydání>        1.1.0.0    bus 1, mqtt 1, vydání 0.0
      HA       <mqtt>.<vydání>              1.1.0      mqtt 1, vydání 0.8
      ```
      
      | Kde | Verze | Kompatibilita | Kde ji uvidíte |
      | --- | --- | --- | --- |
      | Integrace Home Assistant | `1.1.0` | MQTT `1` | hlavička panelu, informace o připojení, WebSocket `version`/`mqtt_compat` |
      | ESP32 master | `1.1.0.0` | bus `1`, MQTT `1` | status `version`/`bus_compat`/`mqtt_compat`, informace o připojení |
      | Firmware modulu | `1.0.1` | bus `1` | inspektor modulu, karta firmwaru, `m<id>v`, UPDI dump |
      
      Integrace porovnává `mqtt_compat` masteru s `MQTT_COMPAT` v `const.py`. Při
      neshodě se zobrazí žluté upozornění, ale normální zobrazení, zrušení OTA ani
      reset modulu to nikdy nezablokuje. Pokud master verzi vůbec nehlásí (starší
      firmware), panel ji označí jako neznámou a nebude předpokládat kompatibilitu.
      Generace sběrnice se zobrazuje pro diagnostiku; Home Assistant s ní přímo
      nemluví.
      
      Karta **MODULE FIRMWARE** ukazuje verzi a generaci sběrnice, kterou každý modul
      skutečně hlásí. Použijte ji jako důkaz, že OTA proběhla: zvyšte `FW_RELEASE` ve
      firmwaru modulu, nahrajte nový `.hex` a po restartu a homogenizaci se na kartě
      musí objevit nová verze. OTA sama odmítne neznámý protokol bootloaderu ještě
      před zápisem první stránky.

- path: README.md
  content: |
      ## Features
      
      - **Sidebar panel** (`Split-Flap OS`) with Control, Apps, Tuning, and Settings
        tabs, plus a live flap preview.
      - **Board auto-detection**: module count comes from the master status payload.
        45 modules become 3×15 and 64 become 4×16. Small displays use a single row.
        The physical frame can be overridden with rows/columns and a per-row module
        layout such as `3,3,1`.
      - **Physical layouts and app availability**: short rows are centred, module IDs
        are assigned in reading order, and data apps are disabled with a reason when
        every row is not wide enough.
      - **Apps** rendered from Home Assistant data where possible:
        clock, date, dashboard, weather, stocks, crypto, NHL scores, MBTA transit,
        countdown, world clock, ISS position, and colour animations.
      - **Playlists** with per-page text, loop control, and saved named playlists.
      - **Animation send orders**: left-to-right, right-to-left, columns, centre-out,
        outside-in, diagonal, random, rain, and spiral.
      - **Tuning UI** for module inspection, home, goto, relative steps, home offsets,
        EEPROM position maps, recording drum indexes, bus scan, sync, and refresh.
      - **Entities and services** so automations can send text, launch apps, and run
        hardware actions without the panel.
      - **Character validation**: text and playlists are checked against each
        module's reported `flap_list` before anything is sent; a missing flap raises
        an error naming the module and character.
      - **Czech localization** of the setup/options flow and service names; the panel
        and entity names remain English.
      - **Backup/restore** of settings, playlists, and the last module snapshot.
      - Only one config entry is allowed, matching the single-master firmware.
      
      ## Requirements
      
      - Home Assistant 2024.11 or newer.
      - The MQTT integration configured and connected to the broker used by the master.
      - SplitFlap Master firmware with these topics:
        - status: `<prefix>/status` (retained, JSON)
        - commands: `<prefix>/command/display`, `sync`, `scan`, `update`, `calibrate`
      - The default prefix is `splitflap`. It is configurable during setup.
      
      ## Installation
      
      ### HACS (custom repository)
      
      1. Add this repository as a HACS **Integration** custom repository.
      2. Install **Split-Flap OS**.
      3. Restart Home Assistant.
      4. Go to **Settings → Devices & services → Add integration → Split-Flap OS**.
      5. Enter the MQTT topic prefix (`splitflap` by default) and a display name.
      
      ### Manual
      
      Copy `custom_components/splitflap_os` into your Home Assistant
      `config/custom_components/` directory and restart. Then add the integration from
      the UI.
      
      The sidebar panel is registered automatically; no Lovelace resource entry is
      needed.
      
      ## Panel
      
      - **Control** — live display, multi-line compose box, colour insert buttons,
        start column, send order, speed, playlist builder, and saved playlists.
      - **Apps** — tap an app to start it; the gear opens the settings that app reads.
      - **Tuning** — module matrix, per-module diagnostics, motor home/goto/step,
        record and position-map controls, and a clickable character map.
      - **Settings** — grouped settings (display, weather, markets, sports, transit,
        time, animations), hardware actions, backup/restore, and connection details.
      
      The panel uses Home Assistant WebSocket commands and does not require a build
      step. It is loaded from `frontend/splitflap-os-panel.js` through `panel_custom`.
      
      ## Entities
      
      | Platform | Entity | Purpose |
      | --- | --- | --- |
      | sensor | Status | Master online/offline plus MQTT metadata |
      | sensor | Module count | Number of detected modules |
      | sensor | Display text | Last non-raw text shown |
      | sensor | Active app | Active app, playlist, or idle |
      | button | Home all | Home every module |
      | button | Scan bus | Full RS485 discovery |
      | button | Sync state | Republish master state / EEPROM sync |
      | button | Refresh modules | Update known modules without a scan |
      | button | Stop display | Stop the app or playlist |
      | text | Set display text | Write text directly from automations |
      | select | App | Start an app or choose Off |
      
      ## Services
      
      All services live under `splitflap_os.*`.
      
      | Service | Description |
      | --- | --- |
      | `send_text` | Send wrapped text with `start`, `style`, `speed`, `stop`, `raw` |
      | `play_playlist` | Play pages with `delay` and `loop` |
      | `start_app` / `stop_app` | Control the app engine |
      | `sync` / `scan` / `update` | Hardware state actions |
      | `calibrate` | Per-module goto/home/step/record/apply/clear_map/get_pos |
      | `home_all` / `record_all` | Bulk calibration helpers |
      | `save_playlist` / `delete_playlist` / `run_saved_playlist` | Playlist management |
      | `set_settings` | Merge and persist settings |
      
      Service `pages` fields accept a real YAML list when called from scripts, or a
      JSON array string when using the UI. `send_text` treats `start` as a 1-based
      column offset. `speed` is forwarded with the display command; the current master
      firmware ignores it and uses its own fixed bus timing.
      
      Before text is published, every module that reports a `flap_list` is checked
      for the characters it will receive. If a flap is missing, the service raises an
      error naming the module and character, and nothing is sent. `play_playlist`
      validates all pages before it starts. Padding spaces are ignored, and modules
      without a reported flap list are skipped because there is no drum to compare
      against.
      
      ## Settings
      
      Settings are stored with Home Assistant's `Store` under the config entry and are
      available from the panel. Important keys include:
      
      - `row_counts`, `rows`, `cols` — the physical display layout. `row_counts` is
        one comma-separated module count per row, for example `3,3,1`. Blank means
        automatic layout. `rows` and `cols` are the frame dimensions; `0` means
        derive them from the detected module count.
      - `ui_scale` — panel preview scale in percent (`50`–`200`, default `100`).
        Increase it to make a small physical display easier to see in the panel.
      - `timezone`, `units`, `page_delay`.
      - `weather_entity` (preferred), `zip_code` + `weather_api_key` (OpenWeather
        fallback).
      - `stocks_list`, `crypto_list`, `sports_teams`.
      - `metro_stop`, `metro_route`, `mbta_api_key`.
      - `countdown_event`, `countdown_target`, `clock_format`, `world_clock_zones`.
      - `anim_effect`, `anim_style`, `anim_speed`.
      
      Weather uses the Home Assistant `weather.get_forecasts` service when an entity is
      selected, so no external API key is required for the normal path. Stocks and
      crypto use Yahoo Finance and CoinGecko respectively. MBTA works without a key at
      low volume; an API key is optional.
      
      ## Physical layout and app availability
      
      The layout describes the real display, not just the number of modules.
      
      [read_files: showing lines 22-161 of 420. Use code_search to locate the part you need and read a window around it, or call read_files again with offset=162 to continue.]
      
      `map[0]` and redefines `homeOffset`. That is the intended way to re-centre flap
      0, not a destructive compatibility write. Older master firmware also sent a
      second `m<id>w0:0`; current firmware does not.
      
      ## Adding an app
      
      1. Add an async provider in `custom_components/splitflap_os/apps/`:
      
         ```python
         async def my_app(engine, now) -> list[Page]:
             return [Page(engine.lines("HELLO", "WORLD", ""), delay=5)]
         ```
      
      2. Describe it with `AppDef` and register it in
         `custom_components/splitflap_os/apps/__init__.py`.
      3. If it has settings, add `SettingField`s and optionally add them to a group in
         `settings.py`.
      
      Providers are called once per display cycle. Slow network calls should use
      `await engine.async_cached(key, ttl, factory)`.
      
      ## Project layout
      
      ```
      custom_components/splitflap_os/
      ├── __init__.py          setup, unload, cleanup
      ├── apps/                app providers and registry
      ├── config_flow.py       single-instance setup and options
      ├── const.py             domain constants
      ├── coordinator.py       MQTT state, normalization, publishing
      ├── engine.py            display loop, playlists, settings, backup
      ├── entity.py            shared entity base
      ├── frontend/            sidebar panel JavaScript
      ├── layout.py            pure text/layout/order/rotation helpers
      ├── manifest.json
      ├── models.py            Page object
      ├── panel.py             static path + panel registration
      ├── runtime.py           runtime lookup helper
      ├── sensor.py / button.py / text.py / select.py
      ├── services.py / services.yaml
      ├── settings.py          grouped settings metadata
      ├── strings.json / translations/en.json
      └── websocket_api.py     panel commands
      ```
      
      `app.py` and `index.html` in the repository root are AdamGMakes' original
      reference implementation. They are not loaded by Home Assistant.
      
      ## Development checks
      
      Home Assistant is not vendored in this repository. Run the checks that do not
      need a full Home Assistant install:
      
      ```bash
      python3 -m py_compile custom_components/splitflap_os/*.py \
        custom_components/splitflap_os/apps/*.py
      for f in $(find custom_components/splitflap_os/frontend -name '*.js'); do node --check "$f"; done
      python3 -m json.tool custom_components/splitflap_os/manifest.json >/dev/null

> _Reasoning_
> Bug: async_stop clears notifications even when called from `async_play_playlist` and `async_start_app`; fine. But `async_stop` is called at the end of non-looping playlist internally? In `_runner`, non-looping sets mode idle directly (not async_stop), leaving _notifications maybe queued but runner exits, idle task not started. Minor.
> 
> Critical bug: `async_notify` calls `_validate_board`, which uses `self._mapped_chars` → `self.layout` and coordinator drums. Fine.
> 
> Critical race: `_run_idle_notifications` finally calls `_restore_display_state` when mode idle. `async_stop` sets mode idle then cancels idle task → restore; then async_stop sets `_current_page=None`, index 0. Fine. But `async_stop` also clears queue before cancel. Good.
> 
> Another bug: `async_stop` calls `_cancel_idle_notifications` before cancelling runner. If idle task is current task? no.
> 
> Bigger issue: in `async_notify`, if mode=="idle" and a runner task is actually still running (mode set idle by non-loop playlist but task not done), `self.running` true so no idle task; runner will exit. Notification stays queued until next notify or app. Edge; acceptable? Could start idle task when runner completes. Add in `_runner` finally: if mode idle and notifications: `_start_idle_notifications()`. But `_stop_event` may be set from prior stop; `_run_idle_notifications` uses stop_event wait for duration → immediately returns. We should reset stop event before idle notifications. `async_notify` idle path: `self._stop_event` may be set (after async_stop resets it, no). For non-loop playlist exit, stop not set. Fine. Add in finally? Hmm keep simple.
> 
> More important: `async_notify` when mode idle but `_idle_notify_task` exists and is showing; append; task loop continues. Good.
> 
> `get_setting` fallback for active app when app has no such key: it returns global settings key if present. Since old flat keys are no longer stored after migration, only if user sets flat via set_settings (rejected). Fine. But `dashboard` provider calls weather which uses ctx.get_setting; works.
> 
> Now `_settings_for_ui` defaults includes only registry defaults; registry defaults = global + app. Good.
> 
> `async_set_settings`: `known` includes `default_drum` etc. Good.
> 
> Panel `_renderSettings`: `_settingsBuilt` set true once. If apps registry changes on integration reload, panel shell reload? `_settingsBuilt` persists, groups same unless version reload; panel is recreated on browser reload. Fine.
> 
> Panel settings app subtab: app groups now 11; `_appSettingsKey` persisted from old ("weather") still exists; if old key "time" no longer exists, falls back first key. Fine.
> 
> But `settings_groups` group `date` has fields; okay.

> Now critical: `_validate_board` in async_notify can reject lowercase notification text? compose_board uppercases text. Good.

> The `Page` import used in `_restore_display_state`; fine.

> Now `_runner` notification drain occurs *before* display; but after `_sleep` returns from notification, it continues where it left. Yes.

> Wait `_drain_notifications` when called from `_sleep` pops all and displays; after it returns, `_sleep` loop recomputes remaining and continues. Good.

"""Translation parity checks for the Home Assistant JSON files.

Run with ``python3 tests/test_translations.py``.  Home Assistant is not needed;
the files are plain JSON.  The panel keeps its own dictionaries in
``frontend/splitflap-os-panel.js`` and mirrors the same key structure there.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import unittest
from typing import Any

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
COMPONENT_DIR = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(HERE), "custom_components", "splitflap_os")
FILES = {
    "strings.json": os.path.join(COMPONENT_DIR, "strings.json"),
    "en.json": os.path.join(COMPONENT_DIR, "translations", "en.json"),
    "cs.json": os.path.join(COMPONENT_DIR, "translations", "cs.json"),
}


def flatten(value: Any, prefix: str = "") -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return dotted leaf paths so two documents can be compared by shape."""

    out: dict[str, Any] = {}
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        for key, child in value.items():
            out.update(flatten(child, f"{prefix}.{key}" if prefix else key))
    else:
        out[prefix] = value
    return out


class TranslationParityTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.documents = {}
        for name, path in FILES.items():
            with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                self.documents[name] = flatten(json.load(handle))

    def test_all_files_have_the_same_keys(self) -> None:
        reference = set(self.documents["strings.json"])
        for name, document in self.documents.items():
            details = sorted(reference - set(document))
            extra = sorted(set(document) - reference)
            self.assertEqual(
                details,
                [],
                f"{name} is missing keys: {details}",
            )
            self.assertEqual(
                extra,
                [],
                f"{name} has extra keys: {extra}",
            )

    def test_every_service_field_has_a_name(self) -> None:
        for name, document in self.documents.items():
            for key, value in document.items():
                if ".services." in f".{key}" and key.endswith(".name"):
                    self.assertTrue(value, f"{name}: {key} is empty")

    def test_english_and_czech_have_no_empty_values(self) -> None:
        for name in ("en.json", "cs.json"):
            for key, value in self.documents[name].items():
                self.assertNotIn(
                    value,
                    (None, ""),
                    f"{name}: {key} is empty",
                )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main(verbosity=2)

"""Version lockstep checks for the Home Assistant integration.

Run with ``python3 tests/test_versions.py``.  Home Assistant is not needed: the
files are read as text and parsed with regular expressions.

The cross-repo version model (two compatibility axes plus per-repo release)
is specified in the slave repository's ``docs/VERSIONING.md``.  This test only
enforces the local half of it: every Home Assistant file must carry the same
``VERSION``, and its major number must equal ``MQTT_COMPAT``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import re
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
COMPONENT_DIR = HERE.parent / "custom_components" / "splitflap_os"
FRONTEND_DIR = COMPONENT_DIR / "frontend"

CONST_FILE = COMPONENT_DIR / "const.py"
MANIFEST_FILE = COMPONENT_DIR / "manifest.json"
CONSTANTS_FILE = FRONTEND_DIR / "constants.js"

# Every ES module import carries ``?v=<version>`` to bust the Home Assistant
# and browser caches.  A stale parameter serves an old module, so all of them
# must match the current version.
IMPORT_PATTERN = re.compile(r'"\.{1,2}/[^"\n]+?\?v=([^"\s]+)"')


def read(path: Path) -> str:
    return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def const_version(text: str) -> str:
    match = re.search(r'^VERSION:\s*Final\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"', text, re.MULTILINE)
    if not match:
        raise AssertionError("const.py: VERSION: Final = \"...\" not found")
    return match.group(1)


def const_mqtt_compat(text: str) -> int:
    match = re.search(r"^MQTT_COMPAT:\s*Final\s*=\s*(\d+)", text, re.MULTILINE)
    if not match:
        raise AssertionError("const.py: MQTT_COMPAT: Final = <int> not found")
    return int(match.group(1))


def manifest_version(text: str) -> str:
    return str(json.loads(text)["version"])


def constants_version(text: str) -> str:
    match = re.search(r'^export const VERSION = "([^"]+)";', text, re.MULTILINE)
    if not match:
        raise AssertionError("frontend/constants.js: export const VERSION not found")
    return match.group(1)


class VersionLockstepTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.const_text = read(CONST_FILE)
        self.version = const_version(self.const_text)
        self.compat = const_mqtt_compat(self.const_text)

    def test_version_is_compatible_with_mqtt_compat(self) -> None:
        match = re.fullmatch(r"(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)", self.version)
        self.assertIsNotNone(
            match,
            f"VERSION {self.version!r} is not MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH",
        )
        major = int(match.group(1))
        self.assertEqual(
            major,
            self.compat,
            f"VERSION major {major} != MQTT_COMPAT {self.compat}",
        )

    def test_manifest_matches_const(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(manifest_version(read(MANIFEST_FILE)), self.version)

    def test_frontend_constants_match_const(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(constants_version(read(CONSTANTS_FILE)), self.version)

    def test_import_query_parameters_match_const(self) -> None:
        stale: list[str] = []
        for path in sorted(FRONTEND_DIR.rglob("*.js")):
            for line_number, line in enumerate(read(path).splitlines(), 1):
                for found in IMPORT_PATTERN.findall(line):
                    if found != self.version:
                        stale.append(f"{path.relative_to(HERE.parent)}:{line_number}: ?v={found}")
        self.assertEqual(stale, [], "stale ES module versions:\n" + "\n".join(stale))

    def test_mqtt_compat_is_one_digit(self) -> None:
        # The slave EEPROM slot composes "<compat>.<release>" and is 8 bytes,
        # so a two-digit generation would no longer fit.
        self.assertTrue(1 <= self.compat <= 9, "MQTT_COMPAT must be 1..9")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main(verbosity=2)

      """Local app discovery.
      
      Every app is a directory under this package::
      
          apps/<id>/manifest.json
          apps/<id>/app.py
      
      Only apps shipped inside the integration are loaded.  Nothing is downloaded
      and no third-party code is executed.  App modules are imported off the event
      loop (the engine calls :func:`load_apps` in an executor), and each app gets a
      narrow :class:`~.common.AppContext` instead of the engine.
      
      A new app appears after reloading the integration, because the registry is
      built during ``async_setup_entry``.
      """
      
      from __future__ import annotations
      
      import importlib.util
      import json
      import logging
      import re
      import sys
      from dataclasses import dataclass
      from datetime import datetime
      from pathlib import Path
      from typing import Any, Awaitable, Callable
      
      from .common import AppContext, AppDef, SettingField
      
      _LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)
      
      _APP_KEY_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$")
      
      PageProvider = Callable[
          [AppContext, datetime], Awaitable[Any]
      ]
      
      
      @dataclass(frozen=True)
      class AppRegistry:
          """Everything derived from the on-disk app manifests."""
      
          apps: tuple[AppDef, ...]
          providers: dict[str, PageProvider]
          groups: list[dict[str, Any]]
          defaults: dict[str, Any]
          keys: frozenset[str]
      
          def app(self, key: str) -> AppDef | None:
              for app in self.apps:
                  if app.key == key:
                      return app
              return None
      
          def provider(self, key: str) -> PageProvider | None:
              return self.providers.get(key)
      
          def app_defs(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
              return [app.as_dict() for app in self.apps]
      
          def settings_for_ui(self, settings: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
              """Return merged defaults plus only keys the registry knows."""
      
              merged = dict(self.defaults)
              merged.update(
                  {key: value for key, value in settings.items() if key in self.keys}
              )
              return merged
      
          def migrate_settings(self, raw: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
              """Move pre-namespacing global keys into every app that declared them.
      
              Older releases stored one flat ``clock_format`` or ``weather_entity``
              key shared by all apps.  Each app now owns its own copy, so the legacy
              value is copied to every app whose manifest declares that local key.
              Values already stored under a namespaced key win.
              """
      
              migrated = dict(raw)
              for app in self.apps:
                  for field in app.fields:
                      local = field.key.split(".", 1)[-1]
                      if field.key not in migrated and local in raw:
                          migrated[field.key] = raw[local]
              return migrated
      
      
      def _field_from_manifest(app_key: str, data: dict[str, Any]) -> SettingField:
          if not isinstance(data, dict):
              raise ValueError("settings entries must be objects")
          local_key = str(data.get("key") or "").strip()
          if not local_key:
              raise ValueError("setting without a key")
      
          visible_when: dict[str, Any] | None = None
          raw_visible = data.get("visible_when")
          if isinstance(raw_visible, dict) and raw_visible.get("key"):
              visible_when = {
                  "key": f"{app_key}.{raw_visible['key']}",
                  # An empty equals value is meaningful ("show when the field is
                  # blank"), so do not use ``or`` here.
                  "equals": raw_visible.get("equals", ""),
              }
      
          options = data.get("options") or ()
          if not isinstance(options, (list, tuple)):
              raise ValueError("setting options must be a list")
      
          def _optional_number(name: str) -> float | None:
              value = data.get(name)
              return float(value) if value is not None else None
      
          return SettingField(
              key=f"{app_key}.{local_key}",
              label=str(data.get("label") or local_key),
              type=str(data.get("type") or "text"),
              options=tuple(str(option) for option in options),
              placeholder=str(data.get("placeholder") or ""),
              default=data.get("default", ""),
              minimum=_optional_number("min"),
              maximum=_optional_number("max"),
              step=_optional_number("step"),
              domain=str(data["domain"]) if data.get("domain") else None,
              help=str(data.get("help") or ""),
              visible_when=visible_when,
          )
      
      
      def _app_from_manifest(manifest: dict[str, Any]) -> AppDef:
          key = str(manifest.get("key") or "").strip()
          if not _APP_KEY_RE.match(key):
              raise ValueError(f"invalid app key: {key!r}")
      
          raw_fields = manifest.get("fields") or []
          if not isinstance(raw_fields, list):
              raise ValueError("fields must be a list")
          fields = tuple(_field_from_manifest(key, item) for item in raw_fields)
      
          modes = manifest.get("modes") or ()
          if not isinstance(modes, (list, tuple)):
              raise ValueError("modes must be a list")
      
          return AppDef(
              key=key,
              name=str(manifest.get("name") or key),
              icon=str(manifest.get("icon") or ""),
              description=str(manifest.get("description") or ""),
              fields=fields,
              default_delay=float(manifest.get("default_delay", 5.0)),
              category=str(manifest.get("category") or "data"),
              min_rows=max(1, int(manifest.get("min_rows", 1))),
              min_cols=max(1, int(manifest.get("min_cols", 1))),
              modes=tuple(str(mode) for mode in modes),
          )
      
      
      def _load_provider(app_dir: Path, app_key: str) -> PageProvider:
          module_path = app_dir / "app.py"
          if not module_path.is_file():
              raise ValueError("app.py is missing")
      
          module_name = f"{__package__}.{app_key}.app"
          spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(module_name, module_path)
          if spec is None or spec.loader is None:
              raise ValueError("app.py could not be imported")
          module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
          # Register before exec so relative imports and dataclasses can resolve
          # the module by name during import.
          sys.modules[module_name] = module
          try:
              spec.loader.exec_module(module)
          except Exception:
              sys.modules.pop(module_name, None)
              raise
      
          provider = getattr(module, "fetch", None)
          if provider is None:
              # Backwards-compatible with the older module layout, where the
              # provider was the module's only public coroutine.
              provider = getattr(module, "provider", None)
          if not callable(provider):
              raise ValueError("app.py must define fetch(context, now)")
          return provider
      
      
      def load_apps(
          apps_dir: str | Path,
          *,
          global_defaults: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
          display_group: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
      ) -> AppRegistry:
          """Discover and import every local app.  Intended for an executor job.
      
          ``global_defaults`` and ``display_group`` come from :mod:`.settings`; the
          engine passes them in so this module does not need to import the settings
          module (which would make the package import order fragile).
          """
      
          root = Path(apps_dir)
          apps: list[AppDef] = []
          providers: dict[str, PageProvider] = {}
      
          for app_dir in sorted(root.iterdir()):
              if not app_dir.is_dir() or app_dir.name.startswith(("_", ".")):
                  continue
              manifest_path = app_dir / "manifest.json"
              if not manifest_path.is_file():
                  continue
              try:
                  manifest = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
                  if not isinstance(manifest, dict):
                      raise ValueError("manifest must be a JSON object")
                  app = _app_from_manifest(manifest)
                  if app.key in providers:
                      raise ValueError(f"duplicate app key: {app.key}")
                  provider = _load_provider(app_dir, app.key)
              except Exception as err:  # noqa: BLE001 - one bad app must not break boot
                  _LOGGER.exception("Skipping Split-Flap OS app %s: %s", app_dir.name, err)
                  continue
              apps.append(app)
              providers[app.key] = provider
      
          apps.sort(key=lambda app: app.key)
          groups: list[dict[str, Any]] = [
              display_group
          ] if display_group else []
          groups.extend(
              {
                  "key": app.key,
                  "name": app.name,
                  "icon": app.icon,
                  "category": "apps",
                  "fields": [field.as_dict() for field in app.fields],
              }
              for app in apps
              if app.fields
          )
      
          defaults: dict[str, Any] = dict(global_defaults or {})
          for app in apps:
              for field in app.fields:
                  defaults[field.key] = field.default
      
          return AppRegistry(
              apps=tuple(apps),
              providers=providers,
              groups=groups,
              defaults=defaults,
              keys=frozenset(defaults),
          )

          async def _sleep(self, seconds: float) -> None:
              """Wait for a page, interrupting the wait for queued notifications.
      
              ``_stop_event`` still stops the loop immediately; a notification sets
              ``_wake_event`` so the remaining delay is paused, the message shown,
              and the wait then resumed for the time that was left.
              """
      
              if seconds <= 0:
                  await asyncio.sleep(0)
                  return
      
              loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
              deadline = loop.time() + seconds
              while True:
                  remaining = deadline - loop.time()
                  if remaining <= 0:
                      return
                  stop_wait = asyncio.create_task(self._stop_event.wait())
                  wake_wait = asyncio.create_task(self._wake_event.wait())
                  _, pending = await asyncio.wait(
                      {stop_wait, wake_wait},
                      timeout=remaining,
                      return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED,
                  )
                  for task in pending:
                      task.cancel()
                  if pending:
                      await asyncio.gather(*pending, return_exceptions=True)
                  if self._stop_event.is_set():
                      return
                  if self._wake_event.is_set():
                      self._wake_event.clear()
                      await self._drain_notifications()
